definition_zh: 想象力；想象；创造力
definition_en: the ability to form pictures and ideas in the mind, including things that are not actually present
core_image: 深夜书桌上散开的草图，窗外的云被画成了飞鱼
scene: 作文题只有一行字，纸上却很快铺满了东西。 Her imagination turned a bare classroom into a ship, and the whole class began to steer it.
sceneCN: 这里 imagination 指「想象力」（第 1 个义项：在脑中造出画面的能力），句意是她的想象把空荡荡的教室变成一艘船，全班开始一起掌舵。画面里有只写一行字的作文题和慢慢填满的纸。

pos.zh: 名词：想象力、想象、创造力

senses.title: The power to form pictures
senses.definition: the ability to create images and situations in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中造出画面与情境的能力
senses.example: Children need imagination more than they need toys.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要想象力胜过需要玩具。
senses.why: The -ation ending names the faculty itself, so the word points to an ability rather than to a single picture.
senses.whyCN: -ation 词尾命名的是能力本身，因此这个词指向一种本领，而非某一幅画面。

senses.title: Something invented in the mind
senses.definition: a product of the mind that has no basis in fact
senses.definitionCN: 头脑造出、并无事实依据之物
senses.example: The monster was pure imagination, he admitted later.
senses.exampleCN: 他后来承认那怪物纯属想象。
senses.why: A faculty word easily slides into the thing the faculty produces, just as writing means both skill and text.
senses.whyCN: 表示能力的词很容易滑向它所产出之物，正如 writing 既指写作技能又指文字。

senses.title: Creative power in art or science
senses.definition: the inventive power behind new designs, stories or theories
senses.definitionCN: 催生新设计、新故事或新理论的创造能力
senses.example: The vaccine grew from years of scientific imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗源自多年科学上的创造力。
senses.why: Inventing and picturing rely on the same act of seeing what is not there, so the word covers both art and discovery.
senses.whyCN: 发明与想象都依赖同一个动作——看见尚不存在之物，于是这个词兼指艺术与发现。

intro.en: Imagination is the Latin noun built on imaginari, to picture to oneself, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: imagination 建立在拉丁语 imaginari（在心中构想）之上的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Imaginari meant to picture something to oneself, active mental seeing rather than mere copying.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imaginari 意为在心头构想某物，是主动的心里观想，而非单纯复制。

items.en: Imaginatio named the faculty that holds such pictures, discussed at length by medieval scholars.
items.cn: imaginatio 命名持有这些画面的能力，中世纪学者对此多有讨论。

items.en: French used imagination for the mind's picturing power, both serious and playful.
items.cn: 法语用 imagination 指心智造图之力，严肃与游戏皆可。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fourteenth century, first in medicine and philosophy.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入，最初见于医学与哲学。

items.en: Romantic writers raised imagination to a creative force, and education took it as a core skill.
items.cn: 浪漫主义作家把想象提升为创造之力，教育也把它视作核心素养。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's other noun-like forms; the near-meaning group gathers powers of the mind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的其他名词性形式；近义组收其他表示心智力气的词。

entries.definition: Pictures in art or writing, near in shape but not the faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术或文学中的意象，形状相近但并非能力。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind, an adjective where this word is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于心中的：本词是名词，它是形容词。

entries.definition: Full of imagination, the adjective built on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 富有想象力的，与本词同基的形容词。

entries.definition: The power to make new things, closer to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 创造新事物的能力，更接近第三个义项。

entries.definition: A scene invented in the mind, often pleasant and impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 脑中虚构的情景，常是愉悦而不可能发生的。

entries.definition: The making of something new, or something made up.
entries.definitionCN: 造出新事物，也可指编造之物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks place the -ation heavy ending beside the lighter verb and adjective forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把沉重的 -ation 词尾与较轻盈的动词、形容词形式并排放。

normal.en: Long words often mirror long ability: five syllables for a power that never runs short.
normal.cn: 长词常对应绵长的能力：五个音节，配一种用不完的本事。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: i-ma-gi-NA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音落在第四音节：i-ma-gi-NA-tion。

normal.en: Its verb is imagine and its adjective imaginative; the ending changes the word's role.
normal.cn: 动词是 imagine，形容词是 imaginative，词尾改变的是词的职务。

normal.en: The root imag- sits inside image, so the power is always about making pictures.
normal.cn: 词根 imag- 就在 image 里，这种能力始终与造画面有关。

normal.en: Say beyond imagination and you name a limit you cannot measure.
normal.cn: 说「超乎想象」，你命名的是一条量不出的界线。

abstract.en: Imagination is not the opposite of knowledge; it is knowledge reaching for what does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 想象并不是知识的反面，而是知识伸手去够还不存在的东西。

abstract.en: A child with a stick and a good imagination owns a horse, a sword and a whole kingdom.
abstract.cn: 一个拿着棍子、想象丰沛的孩子，同时拥有一匹马、一把剑和整个王国。

abstract.en: The word describes a power that grows when used and withers when denied, unlike almost every other faculty.
abstract.cn: 这种能力越用越强、越禁越枯，几乎与所有其他本领都不同。

examples.en: The story caught the imagination of readers everywhere.
examples.cn: 这个故事激发了各地读者的想象。

examples.en: She has a vivid imagination and draws monsters every day.
examples.cn: 她想象力丰富，每天都画怪物。

examples.en: Solving the problem required imagination as much as knowledge.
examples.cn: 解决这个问题既需要知识，也同样需要想象力。

dict_mnemonic.text: imagine 想象 + ation 名词尾——想象的能力，即想象力

root: 拉丁语 imaginari「在心中构想」（词干 imagin-）→ imaginatio，经古法语 imagination 进入英语，近代由文学与教育学定为「想象力」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the power to picture, the products of that power, and its creative force in art and science.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：造画面的能力、这种能力的产物，以及它在艺术与科学中的创造力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sketch pads under a lamp, with clouds redrawn as flying fish.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下摊开的草图本，云被改画成飞鱼。

branches.en: THE FACULTY LINE: the word names a lasting capacity of the mind.
branches.cn: 能力线：这个词命名心智中一种持久的本领。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT LINE: monsters and kingdoms are its output.
branches.cn: 产物线：怪物与王国都是它的产物。

branches.en: THE CREATIVE LINE: designs and theories grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 创造线：设计与理论也从同一根部长出来。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: teachers value it alongside memory and logic.
branches.cn: 学校线：教师把它与记忆、逻辑并列看待。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY LINE: the same power gives both the picture and the fake.
branches.cn: 边界线：同一种能力既给出画面，也给出假象。

intro.en: Imagination is the heaviest member of the image family, built with the Latin noun ending -atio.
intro.cn: imagination 是 image 家族里最重的一员，用拉丁语名词词尾 -atio 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both imaginatio and its verb imaginari are recorded in Latin prose, so no reconstruction is needed.
latinIntro.cn: imaginatio 及其动词 imaginari 在拉丁语散文中均有记录，无需构拟。

items.exampleCN: image 与 imagery 共用此词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或能力的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: 想象力造出了整台机器。
他们的想象各走各的路。

items.example: Imagine a city with no cars.
items.exampleCN: 想象一座没有汽车的城市。
那是个富有想象力的设计。

items.example: The novel is rich in imagery.

definition_zh: 心理的；心理学的；心理层面的；（小说）心理描写的；（优势、战争）心理上的；心理上合适的
definition_en: relating to the mind, to the study of the mind, or to effects that work through feelings rather than physical force
core_image: 打开一个人的头盖，里面不是齿轮而是流动的情绪与念头
scene: 长期睡眠不足会带来心理上的负担。 The study found that long periods of noise produced measurable psychological stress even when hearing was unaffected.
sceneCN: 这里 psychological 是「心理层面的」（第 3 个义项：作用于情绪与精神，而非听觉器官）；句意：研究发现在长时间噪声下，即使听力未受影响，也会产生可测量的心理压力。图中可辨识物件：分贝计、被噪声包围的人形轮廓、下沉的情绪曲线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 心理的；心理学的；心理层面的；心理描写的

senses.title: Belonging to the mind
senses.definition: relating to the mind and its processes of thought, feeling and perception
senses.definitionCN: 与心智及其思维、情感与知觉过程相关
senses.example: Sleep loss has both physical and psychological consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足既有生理后果，也有心理后果。
senses.why: Psyche meant 'breath, soul, mind'. Psychological marks whatever belongs to that inner life rather than to the body's machinery.
senses.whyCN: psychē 意为“气息、灵魂、心智”。psychological 标记属于这种内在生活、而非身体机制的东西。

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.definition: belonging to psychology as an academic or clinical field
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学术或临床领域的心理学
senses.example: The paper appeared in a leading psychological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份顶尖心理学期刊上。
senses.why: Once psychology became a laboratory science in the 19th century, psychological came to mean 'of the discipline', covering experiments, journals and clinics.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪心理学成为实验室科学之后，psychological 开始指“属于该学科的”，涵盖实验、期刊与诊所。

senses.title: Working through feeling
senses.definition: affecting a person through emotions and mental state rather than physical force
senses.definitionCN: 通过情绪与心理状态而非物理力量影响人
senses.example: The threat of redundancy caused psychological harm long before any job was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 裁员的威胁在任何岗位真正消失之前就已造成心理伤害。
senses.why: The word names effects that travel through the mind: fear, shame or anxiety can do damage even when no physical injury occurs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名经由心智传导的影响：恐惧、羞耻或焦虑即使没有身体伤害，也能造成损伤。

senses.title: Based on mental measurement
senses.definition: measured or assessed through mental tests and reported feelings rather than physical instruments
senses.definitionCN: 通过心理测试与自述感受而非物理仪器来测量或评估
senses.example: The trial used psychological scales to rate anxiety before and after treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 试验用心理量表评定治疗前后的焦虑程度。
senses.why: Research needed a word for data that comes from questionnaires and scales, so psychological marks the measuring method as well as the subject.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要为来自问卷与量表的数据找个词，于是 psychological 既标记研究对象，也标记测量方法。

senses.title: An edge in the mind
senses.definition: giving an advantage by affecting confidence, fear or motivation rather than resources
senses.definitionCN: 通过影响信心、恐惧或动机而非资源来取得优势
senses.example: Winning the first set gave the team a psychological advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 赢下第一盘给这支队伍带来了心理优势。
senses.why: Competition uses the adjective for edges that exist only in the mind: the score is level, but one side already feels beaten or emboldened.
senses.whyCN: 竞争用这个形容词指只存在于心里的优势：比分持平，但一方已感到被击败或受到鼓舞。

senses.title: Written from the inside
senses.definition: of a novel or film: focused on inner motives and feelings rather than external action
senses.definitionCN: 指小说或电影聚焦内心动机与感受，而非外部动作
senses.example: Critics praised the novel as a psychological study of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说是对悲伤的心理研究。
senses.why: Literary criticism borrowed the term for works that stay inside a character's mind, where plot matters less than motive.
senses.whyCN: 文学批评借这个词指留在人物内心的作品，在这类作品中情节不如动机重要。

senses.title: The right moment for the mind
senses.definition: of a moment: judged to be the point when people are most ready to accept something
senses.definitionCN: 指被人判断为最易接受某事的时刻
senses.example: He waited for the psychological moment to raise the question of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 他等待心理上最合适的时机提出经费问题。
senses.why: The fixed phrase 'the psychological moment' treats timing as a mental condition: the instant when resistance is lowest and attention highest.
senses.whyCN: 固定说法“心理上的时机”把时机当作一种心理状态：阻力最低、注意最高的那一刻。

senses.title: Fought through the mind
senses.definition: of warfare or tactics: aimed at beliefs, morale and fear instead of physical targets
senses.definitionCN: 指针对信念、士气与恐惧而非物理目标的战争或战术
senses.example: Leaflets and broadcasts were part of a psychological campaign against the garrison.
senses.exampleCN: 传单与广播构成了针对守军的心理战的一部分。
senses.why: Military language uses the adjective when the target is morale: nothing is destroyed, yet the will to fight is attacked directly.
senses.whyCN: 军事语言在目标是士气时用这个形容词：没有东西被摧毁，但战斗意志被直接攻击。

intro.en: Psychological joins Greek psychē, 'breath, soul, mind', with logos, 'word, account, reason', through the Latin-formed psychologia. The -ical ending comes from Latin -icalis and Greek -ikos. The word began as a label for the study of the soul and ended up covering stress, novels, morale and warfare.
intro.cn: psychological 把希腊语 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”与 logos“言说、道理、理性”结合，经由拉丁形式的 psychologia 而来。-ical 词尾来自拉丁 -icalis 与希腊 -ikos。这个词最初是“研究灵魂”的标签，后来覆盖压力、小说、士气与战争。

items.en: Psyche meant 'breath, life, soul'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with the idea of breathing, though no root is proved.
items.cn: psychē 意为“气息、生命、灵魂”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与“呼吸”的观念有关，但没有被证实的词根。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason'. Combined with other stems, -logia named a field of study or a body of discourse.
items.cn: logos 意为“言说、记述、理性”。与其他词干结合时，-logia 命名一个研究领域或一套论述。

items.en: The compound psychologia was coined in Latin by 16th-century scholars for the study of the soul, before any laboratory existed.
items.cn: 复合词 psychologia 由 16 世纪学者在拉丁语中造出，指对灵魂的研究，当时还没有任何实验室。

items.en: English formed psychological from psychology with the adjective suffix -ical, at first meaning 'of the soul or mind'.
items.cn: 英语用形容词后缀 -ical 从 psychology 造出 psychological，最初意为“属于灵魂或心智的”。

items.en: Wundt and others turned psychology into an experimental discipline, and psychological came to cover measurement, tests and clinical practice.
items.cn: 冯特等人把心理学变成实验学科，psychological 随之覆盖测量、测验与临床实践。

items.en: Psychological warfare was named in the two world wars, psychological novels flourished earlier in the century, and the adjective spread to stress, advantage and timing.
items.cn: 心理战在两次世界大战中得名，心理小说在 20 世纪初兴盛，这个形容词又扩散到压力、优势与时机。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from psychology, the adverb and the different-root physiological. The meaning group contrasts mental, emotional and cognitive descriptions.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与 psychology、副词，以及词根不同的 physiological；词义组比较 mental、emotional 与 cognitive 三类描述。

entries.definition: the study of the mind, or a person's mental make-up. It names the field, while psychological describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 对心智的研究，或某人的心理构成。它命名字科，而 psychological 描述属于该学科的东西。

entries.definition: in mental terms. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something affects the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 在心理层面上。它把形容词转为关于如何影响心智的陈述。

entries.definition: relating to the body's functions. It looks parallel but comes from physis 'nature' plus logos, a different stem from psyche.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体功能相关的。它看起来结构平行，却来自 physis“自然”加 logos，词干与 psychē 不同。

entries.definition: relating to the medical treatment of mental illness. It comes from iatreia 'healing', not from logos 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病的医学治疗相关的。它来自 iatreia“治疗”，而非 logos“研究”。

entries.definition: relating to the mind. It is the plain everyday word and often pairs with health and illness, while psychological is more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 与心智相关的。它是平实的日常词，常与健康、疾病搭配，而 psychological 更技术化。

entries.definition: relating to feelings. It covers one part of mental life, while psychological covers the whole inner system.
entries.definitionCN: 与情感相关的。它覆盖心理生活的一部分，而 psychological 覆盖整个内在系统。

entries.definition: relating to thinking, memory and perception. It names the intellectual side rather than feeling or morale.
entries.definitionCN: 与思维、记忆和知觉相关的。它指理智的一面，而非情绪或士气。

entries.definition: existing in a person's own experience. It marks the private side of what psychological studies measure.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于个人自身经验中的。它标记心理研究所测之物的私人一面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into psyche and logos, then let the inner-life picture cover stress, science, novels, advantage, timing and warfare.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 psyche 与 logos，再用内在生活的画面覆盖压力、科学、小说、优势、时机与战争。

normal.en: Split it as psyche + log + ical: mind + study + adjective. Psychological means 'of the study of the mind'.
normal.cn: 拆成 psyche + log + ical：心智、研究、形容词。psychological 意为“关于心智研究的”。

normal.en: Picture a head opened like a room, with feelings drifting around instead of gears.
normal.cn: 想象一个像房间一样打开的头，里面飘着情绪而不是齿轮。

normal.en: Physical harm hits the body; psychological harm hits the same person through fear and shame.
normal.cn: 物理伤害打身体；心理伤害通过恐惧与羞耻打同一个人。

normal.en: A psychological novel stays inside that room, watching motives instead of events.
normal.cn: 心理小说留在那个房间里，看动机而不是看事件。

normal.en: Psychological warfare attacks morale, so the target is that room rather than any building.
normal.cn: 心理战攻击士气，因此目标就是那个房间，而不是任何建筑。

abstract.en: Keep the two Greek halves visible: psyche is the subject, logos is the way of studying it.
abstract.cn: 让两个希腊部分保持可见：psychē 是对象，logos 是研究方式。

abstract.en: Notice that the adjective can describe both a science and a trick: the same word covers journals and warfare.
abstract.cn: 注意这个形容词既能描述科学也能描述手段：同一个词覆盖期刊与战争。

abstract.en: Contrast it with physiological: one studies the mind, the other the body, even though the words look like twins.
abstract.cn: 与 physiological 对照：一个研究心智，一个研究身体，尽管两词看起来像双胞胎。

examples.en: Researchers measured the psychological effects of isolation on long voyages.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了长期航行中隔离对心理的影响。

examples.en: The coach said the early goal gave his players a psychological lift.
examples.cn: 教练说那个早早的进球让球员们在心理上受到鼓舞。

examples.en: The museum mounted a psychological warfare exhibition from the cold war.
examples.cn: 博物馆举办了一场冷战心理战展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“赛可乐鸡扣”：赛场上喝口可乐，鸡血一扣，心理状态立刻不同。

root: 希腊 psychē“气息、灵魂、心智”加 logos“言说、研究”构成 psychologia，加 -ical 为形容词；核心是“属于心智及其研究”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses point to the inner life: a mind that suffers, a science that studies it, an effect that travels through feeling, a scale that measures it, an advantage that lives in confidence, a novel that stays inside it, a moment when it is ready, and a war that attacks it directly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向内在生活：会受苦的心智、研究它的科学、经由情绪传导的影响、测量它的量表、存在于信心中的优势、留在它内部的小说、它准备好的时刻，以及直接攻击它的战争。

core.en: The inner life of a person, and everything that acts on it or measures it.
core.cn: 一个人的内在生活，以及作用于它或测量它的一切。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the mind itself and the discipline that studies it.
branches.cn: 对象：心智本身以及研究它的学科。

branches.en: EFFECT: harm or advantage arrives through feeling, not force.
branches.cn: 影响：伤害或优势经由情绪而非力量到来。

branches.en: MEASURE: scales and tests turn inner states into data.
branches.cn: 测量：量表与测验把内在状态变成数据。

branches.en: FICTION: a narrative stays inside motive rather than action.
branches.cn: 虚构：叙事留在动机内部，而非外部动作。

branches.en: TIMING AND WAR: the mind is either ready to yield or actively attacked.

definition_zh: 狭窄的；狭隘的；勉强的；变窄
definition_en: measuring a small distance from side to side; limited in range or outlook; won or avoided by only a small margin; and, as a verb, to become less wide
core_image: 两堵墙向中间挤过来，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过
scene: 老城的巷子两边砌着高墙，一辆送货车停在巷口，司机探头量了量两侧后视镜。 The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
sceneCN: 这里是「狭窄的」（第 1 个义项：两侧之间距离小）；句意是这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。图中可辨识物件：高墙、后视镜、巷口的货车。

derivatives.zh: 由 narrow 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「勉强地；差一点」
由 narrow 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「狭窄；狭隘」
由 narrow 与 minded 复合而成，义为「心胸狭隘的」

senses.title: Small in width
senses.definition: measuring only a small distance from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧到另一侧的距离很小
senses.example: The alley is too narrow for a truck to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小巷太窄，卡车过不去。
senses.why: Old English nearu described a space with little room across, and that plain physical tightness is the centre of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nearu 描述横向余量很小的空间，这种朴素的物理上的「挤」是后来所有义项的核心。

senses.title: Limited in scope or outlook
senses.definition: limited in range, sympathy or understanding, and not open to other views
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、同情心或理解力上受限，不愿接纳别的看法
senses.example: The debate was framed by a narrow set of questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论被一组狭窄的问题限制住了。
senses.why: A space with little room across becomes a mind with little room for other ideas, so the physical tightness turns into a limit on thought.
senses.whyCN: 横向余量很小的空间，会变成容不下别的想法的心胸，于是物理上的「挤」就转成了对思想的限制。

senses.title: Barely achieved or barely avoided
senses.definition: achieved by only a small margin, or avoided by only a little distance or time
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的差距取得，或只差一点就避开的
senses.example: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
senses.exampleCN: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。
senses.why: When the gap between two outcomes is narrow, the winner passes with almost no room to spare, so the word marks a close result or escape.
senses.whyCN: 当两种结果的间隙很窄时，赢的一方几乎没有余量地挤过去，所以这个词用来标记接近的结果或险境。

senses.title: To become or make less wide
senses.definition: to become less wide, or to reduce the width or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么宽，或把某物的宽度、范围缩小
senses.example: The road narrows sharply after the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了桥之后，路突然变窄。
senses.why: If the adjective names a small width, the verb names the movement toward it: the two sides come closer and the space shrinks.
senses.whyCN: 如果形容词指的是小宽度，动词指的就是朝这个宽度靠拢的过程：两侧靠近，空间缩小。

intro.en: Narrow is a Germanic adjective for tight space, and the deeper root is uncertain; its senses have spread from width to scope and to a close margin.
intro.cn: narrow 是日耳曼语中形容逼仄空间的形容词，更早的词根不确定；义项从宽度扩展到范围，再扩展到微小的差距。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain, and no single reconstructed root for this Germanic adjective is agreed on.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定，学界并未就这个词的原始印欧语词根达成一致。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective narwaz meant narrow or tight, and it is the generally accepted starting point.
items.cn: 一般认为重构的形容词 narwaz 意为狭窄、逼仄，这是普遍接受的起点。

items.en: Old English nearu meant narrow and confined, and it could also name distress or oppression, the feeling of being squeezed.
items.cn: 古英语 nearu 意为狭窄、受拘束，也可指困苦或压迫，也就是被挤住的感觉。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as narwe or narow, and its meaning settled on small width in space.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 narwe 或 narow，词义固定为空间上的宽度小。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective to limited scope and close margins, and forms the verb narrow, with the phrase narrow down.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词扩展到有限的范围与微小的差距，并造出动词 narrow，以及短语 narrow down。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that end in the same -ow sound but have no shared origin; the near-meaning group collects words for tight space and limited range.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 -ow 音结尾、但并无共同来源的词；近义组收表示逼仄空间与有限范围的词。

entries.definition: Too small and crowded for comfort.

entries.definition: Kept within limits, not allowed to spread.

normalIntro.en: The word starts from tight space, and its later senses are that tightness applied to thought, to results and to movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从逼仄的空间起步，后面的义项都是把这种「挤」用到想法、结果和动作上。

normal.en: Old English nearu meant both narrow and oppressed, which shows that tight space and tight feeling were one idea.
normal.cn: 古英语 nearu 既指狭窄也指受压迫，说明空间的挤与感受上的压抑本是同一个概念。

normal.en: Narrow-minded is narrow plus minded, so a small room in the head stands for a small range of ideas.
normal.cn: narrow-minded 是 narrow 加 minded，脑子里的小房间就成了狭窄的想法范围。

normal.en: Narrow escape keeps the picture of passing through a gap with almost no room on either side.
normal.cn: narrow escape 保留了从两侧几乎无余量的缝隙中穿过的画面。

normal.en: Narrow down adds down: the range is pushed smaller and smaller until only one thing is left.
normal.cn: narrow down 加了 down：范围被越压越小，最后只剩一样东西。

normal.en: The verb narrow is simply the adjective put into motion, so it means the sides moving closer together.
normal.cn: 动词 narrow 就是把形容词变成动作，意思是两侧互相靠近。

abstract.en: A narrow street and a narrow mind share one picture: too little room for anything else to pass.
abstract.cn: 狭窄的街道与狭隘的心胸共用一个画面：几乎没有余量让别的东西通过。

abstract.en: A narrow victory is not a small victory but one that barely fitted through the gap.
abstract.cn: 险胜并不是小胜，而是勉强从缝隙里挤过去的一次胜利。

abstract.en: Every sense measures the distance between two edges, whether those edges are walls, ideas or vote counts.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在量两条边之间的距离，无论那两条边是墙、想法还是票数。

examples.en: The lane was too narrow for the van, so the driver backed out slowly.
examples.cn: 这条巷子太窄，货车过不去，司机只好慢慢倒车出来。

examples.en: She won the vote by a narrow margin of two votes.
examples.cn: 她以两票的微弱优势赢得了表决。

examples.en: The path narrows as it climbs towards the ridge.
examples.cn: 小路向山脊爬升时越来越窄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏肉」——两堵墙往中间捏，把肉都挤住了；记住 narrow 是狭窄的、变窄。

root: 古英语 nearu（狭窄的、受拘束的，也可指困苦），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 narwaz；更早的词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small distance between two sides; the senses then apply it to range of thought, to the margin of a result, and to the act of shrinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两侧之间很小的距离；义项再把它用到思想的范围、结果的差距，以及收缩这个动作上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls press inward until a person can only pass sideways through the gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：两堵墙向中间挤压，人只能侧着身子从缝隙里通过。

branches.en: two high walls leaving one narrow lane
branches.cn: 两堵高墙之间只留一条窄巷

branches.en: a van stopping at the mouth of an alley it cannot enter
branches.cn: 货车停在巷口，进不去

branches.en: a list of questions too short to cover the whole problem
branches.cn: 一组问题太窄，盖不住整个问题

branches.en: a vote decided by two ballots out of hundreds
branches.cn: 几百张票里靠两张定输赢

branches.en: a road pinching together as it climbs
branches.cn: 道路向上延伸时逐渐收窄

intro.en: The entry is held together by the Old English adjective, its English verb, and the endings and compounds built on the same short base.
intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语形容词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在同一词基上的词尾与复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and its deeper root is uncertain, so no reliable Latin cognate is recorded and none is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，更早的词根不确定，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，所以这里不列。

definition_zh: 丧失；损失；亏损；死亡；减少
definition_en: the fact of no longer having something, the money lost in business, or a decrease in amount
core_image: 一只抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的位置空着，只剩一圈浅浅的印痕
scene: 抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的格子空着，只留下一圈浅浅的印痕。 The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
sceneCN: 抽屉里原本放手表的位置空着，只剩印痕；句中的 loss 指「不再拥有某物这一事实」（第 1 个义项：失去占有或拥有）。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、空表位、圆形印痕、旧钥匙、灰尘；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: No longer having something
senses.definition: the fact or experience of no longer having something that one had
senses.definitionCN: 不再拥有曾经拥有之物的这一事实或经历
senses.example: The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 老作坊的失去对村庄的打击比任何人预想的都重。
senses.why: The word names the state left behind when a possession or condition is no longer there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指某物或某种状态不在之后留下的那个空缺状态。

senses.title: A person or thing that is missed
senses.titleCN: 被怀念、被惋惜的人或物
senses.definition: a person or thing whose absence is felt as a deprivation by a group
senses.definitionCN: 其缺席被群体感受为缺失的人或物
senses.example: The retired teacher was a great loss to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休教师对学校是一大损失。
senses.why: Instead of the event of losing, the word can name the thing whose absence is felt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指「失去」这件事，而指那个缺席被感受到的人或物。

senses.title: Money lost in business
senses.definition: the amount by which spending exceeds income in a business or year
senses.definitionCN: 企业或年度中支出超过收入的金额
senses.example: The airline reported a loss for the third year running.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司连续第三年报告亏损。
senses.why: Accounting reverses the idea of gain: what should have come back did not, and the shortfall is the loss.
senses.whyCN: 会计把收益的观念反过来：本该回来的没有回来，缺掉的那部分就是亏损。

senses.title: The death of someone close
senses.definition: the death of a relative or friend, experienced as bereavement
senses.definitionCN: 亲属或朋友的死亡，被视为丧亲之痛
senses.example: She took a long leave after the loss of her father.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲去世后，她请了很长的假。
senses.why: Death is the most absolute form of no longer having someone, so the word serves as its ordinary, gentle name.
senses.whyCN: 死亡是「不再拥有某人」最绝对的形式，因此这个词成了它平常而温和的说法。

senses.title: A decrease in amount or intensity
senses.definition: a reduction in quantity, energy or intensity as something escapes or fades
senses.definitionCN: 随着某物逸出或衰减，数量、能量或强度上的减少
senses.example: Insulation cut heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿过墙壁的热量散失。
senses.why: Physics treats escaping heat as something that leaves the system, which is a loss to the system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把逸出的热视为离开系统的某物，对系统而言就是损失。

senses.title: Failure to win a contest
senses.definition: a defeat in a game, election or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或竞争中落败
senses.example: It was their third loss of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这是他们本赛季的第三场失利。
senses.why: A defeat is the loss of a winning position, and sport shortened the phrase to the single word.
senses.whyCN: 失败就是失去获胜的位置，体育语境把这个短语缩短成一个词。

senses.title: An insured event or sum
senses.titleCN: 保险中的损失事件或金额
senses.definition: the damage or sum that an insurer agrees to cover under a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单同意赔付的损害或金额
senses.example: The policy covered the loss of the cargo at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 保单承保了海上货物的损失。
senses.why: Insurance exists to price misfortune, so the word becomes a technical term for the event and its cost.
senses.whyCN: 保险的存在就是为不幸定价，因此这个词成了指事件及其代价的技术用语。

senses.title: The gap left by something valuable
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：珍贵之物消失后留下的空缺
senses.definition: the emptiness or deficit that remains after something valuable disappears
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵之物消失之后留下的空虚或欠缺
senses.example: The loss of trust was harder to repair than the loss of money.
senses.exampleCN: 信任的丧失比金钱的损失更难修补。
senses.why: Generalised, the word names any absence that registers as a deficit, whether the thing was money, heat, a person or trust.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，这个词指任何被感受为欠缺的缺席，无论所失之物是金钱、热量、人还是信任。

intro.en: Loss comes from Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem also seen in the verb lose; it has no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loss 来自古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，其日耳曼语词干也见于动词 lose；这个词没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form meaning 'breaking up, loss', related to Old Norse los 'the breaking up of an army'.
items.cn: 这个名词可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「瓦解、丧失」的形式，与古诺尔斯语 los「军队溃散」相关。

items.en: Old English los meant 'loss, destruction, ruin', and the related verb losian meant 'to be lost, perish'.
items.cn: 古英语 los 意为「丧失、毁灭、毁坏」，相关动词 losian 意为「失踪、灭亡」。

items.en: In Middle English the noun settled into its modern spelling and the verb separated into lose, so the pair now differ in form and sound.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，名词固定为现代拼写，动词则分立为 lose，于是这对词在形与音上都分开了。

items.en: The commercial sense of a shortfall in the accounts developed in the sixteenth century alongside double-entry bookkeeping.
items.cn: 账目中出现缺口的商业义在十六世纪随复式记账一同发展。

items.en: Insurance made the word a term for a covered event, and sport made it a count of defeats; both usages spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 保险使这个词成为「承保事件」的术语，体育使它成为失败次数的计量；两种用法都在近代普及。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed, and the exact dates of the financial and insurance senses are not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：更早的印欧词根属重构形式，财务义与保险义的确切年代亦未得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds the forms of the same Germanic stock, including one that drifted to a different meaning; group two holds words for damage, shortfall and defeat.
note.cn: 第一组同出日耳曼语词干，其中一个漂移到了别的意思；第二组指损害、缺口与失败。

entries.definition: To stop having something; the noun names the state, the verb names the event, and their spellings must not be swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 失去某物；名词指状态，动词指事件，两者的拼写不可混用。

entries.definition: The past participle and an adjective meaning missing or unable to find the way.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，也作形容词，意为丢失的或迷路的。

entries.definition: A person who loses, especially one who fails to win; it names a person, not an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指失败的人，尤指未能获胜者；指人而非金额。

entries.definition: From the same Germanic root meaning 'free, loose', but it means 'not tight' and is not a synonym of loss.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「自由、松开」的日耳曼词根，但意为「不紧的」，并非 loss 的同义词。

entries.definition: Harm to a thing that reduces its value or usefulness; loss is the value that is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 对物品造成的损害，降低其价值或用途；loss 指已经失去的价值。

entries.definition: The amount by which something falls short, especially in public accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不足的数额，尤指公共账目中的缺口。

entries.definition: A gradual decrease in amount or quality; it describes a process, while loss can be a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的逐渐下降；描述过程，而 loss 可以是一次事件。

entries.definition: The state of being beaten in a battle, game or election; it is narrower than loss.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中被击败的状态；比 loss 更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Germanic history, the real family and the real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的日耳曼语演变、真实词族与真实搭配。

normal.en: The old noun meant 'breaking up': something that was whole is now apart or gone.
normal.cn: 这个旧名词意为「瓦解」：原本完整的东西现在散开或消失了。

normal.en: The family runs lose, lost, loser, loss, lossless, lossy.
normal.cn: 词族包括 lose、lost、loser、loss、lossless、lossy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: at a loss, make a loss, cut losses, weight loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义：困惑或亏本、亏损、及时止损、体重下降。

normal.en: Loss is the state; lose is the event.
normal.cn: loss 是状态，lose 是事件。

normal.en: Accounting sets loss against profit, and sport sets it against a win.
normal.cn: 会计把亏损与利润相对，体育把失利与胜利相对。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer with one empty slot where something used to sit every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，其中一个格子空了，那里原本每天都放着东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that lets warmth escape through it all winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙，整个冬天都让暖意从里面溜走。

abstract.en: Picture a column in a ledger that should have a number and has none.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿里一栏本该有数字，却空着。

examples.en: The loss of the harvest left the family short of cash.
examples.cn: 收成的损失让这家人现金短缺。

examples.en: Insurers estimate the loss before they settle the claim.
examples.cn: 承保人在理赔之前先估算损失。

examples.en: The team never recovered from that early loss.
examples.cn: 这支队伍始终没能从赛季初的那场失利中恢复过来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落了（loss）就找不回」——东西掉了、钱亏了、人走了，都叫丧失

root: 古英语 los（丧失、毁灭），属日耳曼语源，与动词 lose 同出一系；更早的印欧词根属重构形式，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one absence: something that was there is no longer, and the word then names the thing missed, the money short, a death, an escaping quantity, a defeat, an insured event and finally any deficit at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺席展开：原本在那里的东西不在了；这个词再指被惋惜的对象、账上的缺款、死亡、逸出的量、一场失利、承保事件，最后指任何欠缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty place in a drawer where something used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里一个原本放着东西的空位。

branches.en: ABSENCE: the event of losing and the thing whose absence is felt are two sides of one empty place.
branches.cn: 缺席：失去的事件与缺席被感受的对象，是同一个空位的两面。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS: the money that should have come back did not, and the gap is counted as a loss.
branches.cn: 账目：本该回来的钱没有回来，这个缺口就被计为亏损。

branches.en: DEATH: the most absolute absence gets the gentlest name.
branches.cn: 死亡：最绝对的缺席用了最温和的名称。

branches.en: MEASURED ABSENCE: escaping heat and insured cargo are both quantities that leave and must be priced.
branches.cn: 可量的缺席：逸出的热与承保的货物，都是离开并被定价的量。

branches.en: CONTEST AND GENERALITY: a defeat is the loss of a winning position, and any deficit repeats the same shape.
branches.cn: 竞争与泛化：失利是失去获胜位置，任何欠缺都重复同一形状。

intro.en: Loss is a native Germanic noun with no prefix and no Latin root; its ending marks a state rather than an act.
intro.cn: loss 是本族日耳曼名词，既无前缀也无拉丁词根；其词尾标记一种状态，而非一个动作。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the Germanic noun los and the verb lose supply the whole family, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先；日耳曼名词 los 与动词 lose 提供整个词族，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The old noun named a breaking apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个旧名词指「散开、瓦解」。

items.example: The verb and noun split in form.
items.exampleCN: 动词与名词在形式上分了家。

items.example: Losses are counted one by one.
items.exampleCN: 亏损是一笔一笔计数的。

items.meaning: the state of no longer having

items.example: The lost keys turned up years later.
items.exampleCN: 丢失的钥匙多年后被找到。

items.example: The loser of the final took the prize money.
items.exampleCN: 决赛的失利者拿走了奖金。

items.example: The file was compressed in a lossy way.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件以有损方式压缩。

definition_zh: 身体上；体力上；体格上；物质上；按物理规律地；实际地；亲自地；在物理空间中地；有形地
definition_en: in a way that concerns the body, the material world, or the laws of physics, or in person rather than in thought or at a distance
core_image: 身体撞到墙时的那一声闷响，和随之而来的一阵疼
scene: 医生说这项检查要看他的体力，而不只是看化验单。 The test asks whether he is physically able to lift those boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 physically 是「体力上」（第 2 个义项：就身体的力量与能力而言）；句意：这项检查要确认他在体力上能不能搬动那些箱子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 身体上；体力上；物质上；按物理规律地；亲自地

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 身体的；物质的；物理的；体检

senses.title: In the body
senses.definition: in a way that involves or affects the body, as opposed to the mind or the emotions
senses.definitionCN: 以涉及或影响身体的方式，相对于心智或情感
senses.example: After the crash he was shaken but not physically hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车之后他受了惊，但身体没有受伤。
senses.why: Greek physis is 'nature', the growing body. Physical first meant 'natural' and then 'bodily'; physically marks the place where the wall is met by flesh rather than by thought.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 是“自然”，即生长着的身体。physical 先表示“自然的”，再表示“身体的”；physically 标记的是墙被肉而不是被思想撞到的那个地方。

senses.title: In terms of bodily strength
senses.definition: with regard to a person's strength, stamina, or ability to do bodily work
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人的力量、耐力或从事体力工作的能力而言
senses.example: The job is physically demanding but not technically hard.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作对体力要求高，技术上却不难。
senses.why: The body is also a tool with a capacity. This sense measures that capacity, which is why a task can be physically hard while being mentally easy.
senses.whyCN: 身体也是一件有容量的工具。这个义项测量这种容量，所以一项任务可以体力上很难、脑力上却很简单。

senses.title: In build or appearance
senses.definition: with regard to the shape, size, or visible condition of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人身体的形状、大小或可见状态而言
senses.example: He looked physically stronger than he had in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他看起来比春天时体格更强壮。
senses.why: The wall's sound tells you something about the body that hit it. Here physically describes the body as an object others can see and measure.
senses.whyCN: 撞墙的声音能说明撞上去的身体是什么样。这里的 physically 把身体描述成他人能看见、能测量的对象。

senses.title: In the material world
senses.definition: in a material or tangible way, as opposed to symbolically, legally, or in thought
senses.definitionCN: 以物质的、可触摸的方式，相对于象征、法律或思想层面
senses.example: The two offices are physically separate but share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个办公室在物理空间上是分开的，却共用一份预算。
senses.why: From the body the word widens to matter in general. Anything that occupies space and can be bumped into counts as physically real, even if it is not alive.
senses.whyCN: 从身体开始，这个词扩展到一般物质。任何占据空间、能被撞到的东西都算物理上真实，即使它不是活的。

senses.title: According to the laws of physics
senses.definition: in a way that obeys, or is explained by, physical laws such as conservation of energy or causality
senses.definitionCN: 以遵守或被物理规律（如能量守恒或因果性）解释的方式
senses.example: A perpetual motion machine is physically impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 永动机在物理上是不可能的。
senses.why: Here the word invokes the discipline, not the body. Physically impossible means the wall cannot be walked through, no matter how strong the will.
senses.whyCN: 这里调用的是学科，而不是身体。physically impossible 意味着无论意志多强，墙都穿不过去。

senses.title: Actually, not merely on paper
senses.titleCN: 实际存在而非纸面上的
senses.definition: in actual fact, so that something exists or happens rather than being only planned or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 在事实上，使某物真实存在或发生，而不只是被计划或被声称
senses.example: The backup site exists physically, not only in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 备份站点是实际存在的，不只存在于计划里。
senses.why: A plan is weightless. Physically real means the thing can be visited, weighed, or unplugged, which is the test the word applies to claims.
senses.whyCN: 计划没有重量。physically real 意味着这东西可以被走访、称重或拔掉电源，这就是这个词对声明所用的检验。

senses.title: In person, not remotely
senses.definition: by being present in the same place, rather than by phone, letter, or network
senses.definitionCN: 通过身处同一地点，而不是通过电话、信件或网络
senses.example: The witness must appear physically before the court.
senses.exampleCN: 证人必须亲自出庭。
senses.why: A voice on a wire has no body. Physically present restores the wall and the room: the person can be seen, touched, and held to account in one place.
senses.whyCN: 电线里的声音没有身体。physically present 把墙和房间还回来：人能被看见、被触到，并在同一个地方被追究。

senses.title: At a point in space
senses.definition: in a particular location in space, as opposed to being distributed, virtual, or undefined
senses.definitionCN: 位于空间中的某个特定位置，相对于分散、虚拟或位置不明
senses.example: The servers are physically in Frankfurt but logically in the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 这些服务器物理上位于法兰克福，逻辑上却在“云”里。
senses.why: The word insists on coordinates. A cloud has no address until someone points to a building, and physically is the adverb that points.
senses.whyCN: 这个词坚持要坐标。云没有地址，直到有人指向一栋楼，而 physically 就是那只指过去的手。

senses.title: In a tangible form
senses.definition: in a form that can be touched or handled, such as a printed copy or a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 以能够触摸或拿取的形式，如印刷副本或实物
senses.example: The archive keeps the files physically as well as digitally.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆既保存数字文件，也保存实体文件。
senses.why: A file can be a ghost in a machine. Physically kept means there is paper you can drop, which is the oldest test of whether something is really there.
senses.whyCN: 文件可以是机器里的幽灵。以物理形态保存下来，意味着有可以掉在地上的纸，这是检验某物是否真的存在的最古老办法。

intro.en: Physically is physical plus -ly. Physical comes from Latin physicus 'natural, of nature', from Greek physikos, from physis 'nature'. Physis derives from phyein 'to bring forth, grow', so the oldest sense is not 'body' but 'what grows by itself'. English first used physical for medicine and natural things, then for the body, and only later for the science of physics.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 来自拉丁 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，出自希腊 physikos，再上溯 physis“自然”。physis 又出自 phyein“产生、生长”，所以最古老的意义不是“身体”，而是“自己长出来的东西”。英语最早用 physical 指医药与自然事物，之后指身体，再往后才指物理学。

items.en: Physis means 'nature, natural form, growth'. The verb phyein means 'to bring forth, grow'. The physical is therefore first of all the growing world, not the body as opposed to the mind.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然、自然形态、生长”。动词 phyein 意为“产生、生长”。所以 physical 首先是生长着的世界，而不是与心智相对的身体。

items.en: Physicus in Latin means 'natural, of nature', and also 'a natural philosopher'. English physical enters in the 14th century with the sense 'medicinal, healing', since medicine studied natural bodies.
items.cn: 拉丁 physicus 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“自然哲学家”。英语 physical 在 14 世纪进入，义为“医药的、治疗性的”，因为医学研究的是自然身体。

items.en: The sense 'bodily, of the body' becomes common, and the noun physics settles as the name of the science of matter and motion.
items.cn: “身体的、肉体的”这一义项在 16 世纪变得常见，名词 physics 则固定为研究物质与运动的科学名称。

items.en: Physically extends from the body to matter in general and to the laws of nature: physically impossible, physically separate.
items.cn: physically 从身体扩展到一般物质与自然规律：物理上不可能、物理上分开。

items.en: The adverb is the plain -ly form of physical. No new meaning is added: it turns 'of the body or of matter' into 'in the body or in matter'.
items.cn: 副词是 physical 的规则 -ly 形式。没有增加新意义：它把“身体或物质的”变成“在身体上或在物质中”。

items.en: Fiscal looks close but comes from Latin fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it means 'of public money'. Physique shares the physis root but names the shape of the body. Physician also shares physis, since medicine was the study of nature.
items.cn: fiscal 看起来相近，却来自拉丁 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以意为“财政的”。physique 共享 physis 词根，却指身体的形状。physician 也共享 physis，因为医学本是对自然的研究。

note.en: The first group separates the physis family from the fiscal trap. The second group compares bodily, materially, tangibly, and actually, the four adverbs closest to physically.
note.cn: 第一组把 physis 词族与 fiscal 陷阱分开。第二组比较 bodily、materially、tangibly、actually，这四个副词最接近 physically。

entries.definition: relating to the body, to matter, or to physics. The adverb only turns this into a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体、物质或物理学有关的。副词只是把它变成一种方式。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a person's body. It is a noun, so it names the body's form rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形状与体格。它是名词，命名身体形态而非行为方式。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. It shares physis because medicine was once the study of natural bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。它共享 physis，因为医学曾是对自然身体的研究。

entries.definition: relating to public money, taxes, and budgets. Its root is fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it has no bodily or physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与公共资金、税收和预算有关的。它的词根是 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以没有身体或物理含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially as opposed to the mind. It is narrower than physically, which also covers matter and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指相对于心智。它比 physically 窄，后者也覆盖物质与物理学。

entries.definition: in a way that concerns matter or material wealth. Its 'physical' sense is about stuff; its other sense is about money.
entries.definitionCN: 在涉及物质或物质财富的方式上。它的“物理”义关乎东西，另一义则关乎金钱。

entries.definition: in a way that can be touched or clearly perceived. It is the touchable side of physically, not the legal or logical one.
entries.definitionCN: 以可触摸或清楚感知的方式。它是 physically 可触摸的一面，而不是法律或逻辑的一面。

entries.definition: in fact, really. It contrasts with what is said or expected, while physically contrasts with what is mental or virtual.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上、真的。它与所言或所期待相对，而 physically 与心智或虚拟相对。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: physis 'nature', phyein 'grow', Latin physicus, the 14th-century medicinal sense, and the fiscus trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：physis“自然”、phyein“生长”、拉丁 physicus、14 世纪的医药义，以及 fiscus 陷阱。

normal.en: Physis is 'nature, growth': physical first meant 'natural', and only later 'bodily'.
normal.cn: physis 是“自然、生长”：physical 先表示“自然的”，后来才表示“身体的”。

normal.en: The adverb is just -ly: physically means 'in the body or in matter', the same relation with a different position.
normal.cn: 副词只是 -ly：physically 意为“在身体上或在物质中”，关系相同，位置不同。

normal.en: Medicine gave the word its early home, which is why physician and physical share a root.
normal.cn: 医学给了这个词早期归宿，所以 physician 与 physical 共享词根。

normal.en: A plan has no weight; physically real means you can go there and put your hand on it.
normal.cn: 计划没有重量；physically real 意味着你能走过去把手放上去。

normal.en: Fiscal looks like a cousin but comes from fiscus 'treasury'; money is not matter.
normal.cn: fiscal 看起来像表亲，却出自 fiscus“国库”；钱不是物质。

abstract.en: The sound of a body hitting a wall is the oldest proof that there is a wall.
abstract.cn: 身体撞上墙的声音，是“墙确实存在”最古老的证据。

abstract.en: A voice on a wire can lie about where it is; a body in a chair cannot.
abstract.cn: 电线里的声音可以谎报自己在哪；椅子上的身体不行。

abstract.en: A cloud is a place until someone asks where its buildings are.
abstract.cn: 云是一个地方，直到有人问它的楼在哪里。

examples.en: The tablet is physically identical to the one sold last year.
examples.cn: 这台平板与去年出售的那台在物理上完全相同。

examples.en: She was physically exhausted after the climb.
examples.cn: 爬完之后她身体极度疲惫。

examples.en: The director was physically present at the signing.
examples.cn: 签署时董事亲自到场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲兹克利」——身体“菲”常实在地撞到墙上，发出一声“兹”，疼是真的 → physically 身体上；物质上；物理上（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 physicus「自然的」，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis「自然」，再上溯 phyein「产生、生长」；后缀 -ly 构成副词。核心是「身体撞到墙时那声闷响，以及随之而来的疼」。同族含 physical、physics、physique、physician；fiscal（fiscus「国库」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of physically all begin with a body meeting the world. What changes is the aspect in view: the flesh, the strength, the build, matter in general, the laws of nature, actual existence, presence in person, location in space, or a tangible copy.
sensesIntro.cn: physically 的九个义项都从“身体与世界相遇”开始。变化的是所看的侧面：肉、力量、体格、一般物质、自然规律、实际存在、亲自到场、空间位置，还是一份有形的副本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the dull sound of a body hitting a wall, and the pain that proves the wall is there.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体撞到墙时的那声闷响，以及证明墙确实存在的那阵疼。

branches.en: THE BODY: flesh that can be hurt, strength that can be spent, and a build that can be seen.
branches.cn: 身体：会被伤到的肉、会被消耗的力量，以及看得见的体格。

branches.en: MATTER AND FORM: the material world at large, and objects that can be touched or printed.
branches.cn: 物质与形式：广义的物质世界，以及可触摸或可印刷的实物。

branches.en: THE LAWS: what physics permits or forbids, regardless of desire.
branches.cn: 规律：物理学允许或禁止什么，与愿望无关。

branches.en: REAL AND LOCATED: actual existence rather than plans, and a point with real coordinates.
branches.cn: 真实且有位置：实际存在而非计划，以及有真实坐标的地点。

branches.en: PRESENT IN PERSON: a body in the room rather than a voice on a wire.
branches.cn: 亲自到场：房间里的身体，而不是电线里的声音。

intro.en: Physically is physical + -ly. Physical is Latin physicus, from Greek physikos and physis 'nature'. The family is unusual because it produced three separate English words from one root: physical, physics, and physician.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 是拉丁 physicus，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis“自然”。这个词族不寻常之处在于，同一个词根产生了三个各自独立的英语词：physical、physics、physician。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is physicus 'natural, of nature', also used as a noun for a natural philosopher, and physica 'natural things, natural science'. Greek supplied physis and physikos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，也作名词指自然哲学家，以及 physica“自然事物、自然科学”。希腊语提供了 physis 与 physikos。

items.meaning: in the body, in matter, or according to physics
items.meaningCN: 在身体上、在物质中，或按物理规律（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two buildings are physically joined.
items.exampleCN: 这两栋楼在物理上是相连的。

items.meaning: of the body, of matter, or of physics
items.meaningCN: 身体的、物质的或物理学的
items.example: Physical evidence was collected at the site.
items.exampleCN: 现场收集到了实物证据。

items.structure: Greek ta physika 'natural things', via Latin physica
items.meaning: the science of matter, energy, and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学；物理学
items.example: Physics explains why the bridge holds.
items.exampleCN: 物理学解释了这座桥为什么撑得住。

items.meaning: the build and shape of a body

items.structure: Old French fisicien, from Latin physicus
items.example: The physician ordered a chest X-ray.
items.exampleCN: 医生要求做胸部 X 光检查。

items.meaning: the quality of being bodily or tangible
items.example: The dance stresses weight and physicality.
items.exampleCN: 这段舞蹈强调重量与身体感。

items.meaning: treatment by movement and physical means
items.meaningCN: 用运动与物理手段进行的治疗；物理疗法
items.exampleCN: 物理治疗让他的肩膀恢复了。

items.meaningCN: 与公共资金有关的；财政的（fiscus 国库）
items.example: The fiscal year ends in March.

items.structure: Old French fisique < Latin physica < Greek physike 'natural science, medicine'
items.meaning: medicine or the art of healing (archaic); to treat with medicine
items.meaningCN: 药；医术（古旧用法）；用药物治疗
items.example: The old herbals list a physic for fever.
items.exampleCN: 古旧的草药书里列有一种退烧的药。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective and noun, from Greek physikos
latinEntries.meaning: natural, of nature; a natural philosopher
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自然的、属于自然的；自然哲学家
篮子、国库（与 physis 无关）

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的；显眼的；（古义）常见的
definition_en: so clear or easy to see that it needs no explanation; standing openly in view
core_image: 一块石头正挡在必经之路中央，迎面撞上，想不看都难
scene: 从对岸都能看见坝体上的裂缝。 The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
sceneCN: 这里 obvious 是「一眼可见、无法忽略」（第 2 个义项：显而易见）；句意：即使从对岸看，堤坝上的裂缝也一目了然。图中可辨识物件：坝体上的裂缝、渗出的水流、对岸的观察者、手中的望远镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；一目了然的

collocations.zh: 说人人都知道的事；多此一举地明说

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: In the way: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 挡在路上：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the literal Latin sense, placed directly in someone's path so as to meet them face to face
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，指正处在某人前行的路上，与对方迎面相遇
senses.example: In Latin, an obvius thing was one that lay in your way and met you head-on.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，obvius 的东西就是横在你路上、与你迎面相遇的东西。
senses.why: Latin obvius came from obviam, 'in the way': ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'. The first picture is a physical obstacle standing in the road.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 出自 obviam“在路上”：ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）。最初的画面就是一件挡在路中的实体障碍。

senses.title: Plain to see: impossible to miss
senses.definition: visible at once, without searching and without being told
senses.definitionCN: 一眼就能看见，既不用寻找，也不用别人告知
senses.example: The crack in the dam was obvious even from the far bank.
senses.exampleCN: 即使从对岸看，坝体上的裂缝也一目了然。
senses.why: Something standing in the road meets the eye before the mind has time to search for it. This is the 'plain to see' sense recorded from the 1630s.
senses.whyCN: 挡在路上的东西会在脑子来得及寻找之前先撞进眼睛，这就是 17 世纪 30 年代记录下来的“显而易见”义。

senses.title: Easy to understand: no explanation needed
senses.definition: so clear that the mind grasps it immediately, without a chain of reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到脑子立刻就能抓住，不需要一连串推理
senses.example: The rule was obvious once the teacher gave a single example.
senses.exampleCN: 老师只举了一个例子，这条规则就变得明明白白。
senses.why: The road here is the road of thought: an idea that lies across the mind's path is reached without a detour, so understanding feels immediate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的路是思维之路：横在思路上的想法不必绕道就能抵达，于是理解显得毫不费力。

senses.title: Open and unconcealed: not hidden
senses.definition: not concealed or disguised; showing plainly what is actually there
senses.definitionCN: 没有隐藏或伪装，把实际存在的东西直接显露出来
senses.example: His disappointment was obvious to everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌边每个人都看得出他的失望。
senses.why: Latin obvius also meant 'open, exposed'. What is exposed is literally placed in front of the eyes, so there is nothing left to hide behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obvius 还兼有“敞开、暴露”的意思。被暴露的东西就摆在眼前，已经没有可以遮挡的余地。

senses.title: The obvious choice: what anyone would pick
senses.titleCN: 不二之选：谁都会挑的那个
senses.definition: the answer or option so natural that no other seems worth considering
senses.definitionCN: 自然到让人觉得别的选项都不值一提的答案或选择
senses.example: For a first bicycle, the obvious choice is a small, cheap one.
senses.exampleCN: 第一辆自行车，明摆着的选择是买一辆小而便宜的。
senses.why: When only one option stands in the road ahead, it looks like the only road there is; what is plainly visible becomes what is expected.
senses.whyCN: 当前方路上只立着一个选项，它看起来就是唯一的路；看得见的东西于是变成了理所当然的东西。

senses.title: Barefaced: an obvious lie or mistake
senses.titleCN: 赤裸裸：明摆着的谎言或错误
senses.definition: used of faults so plain that no one could pretend not to see them
senses.definitionCN: 用于明显到谁也无法假装看不见的过失
senses.example: The excuse was an obvious lie, and nobody at the meeting believed it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个借口是赤裸裸的谎言，会上没人相信。
senses.why: A falsehood that stands in plain sight is shameless: the visibility itself becomes the accusation, so obvious adds contempt in this use.
senses.whyCN: 摆在明处的假话是无耻的：可见性本身成了指控，因此这一用法里的 obvious 带上了轻蔑。

senses.title: Obsolete: frequently met with, commonplace
senses.titleCN: 古义：常见的、司空见惯的
senses.definition: the earliest recorded sense, 'often encountered, ordinary', now no longer in use
senses.definitionCN: 最早记录的义项“经常遇到、平常”，今已不再使用
senses.example: Early writers used obvious for a sight so common that it drew no comment.
senses.exampleCN: 早期作家用 obvious 形容常见到无人置评的景象。
senses.why: A thing met again and again on the road stops being noticed at all. The 1580s sense was 'frequently met with', and modern English dropped that branch.
senses.whyCN: 在路上反复遇到的东西会彻底失去存在感。16 世纪 80 年代的义项正是“常常遇到”，现代英语丢掉了这条分支。

senses.title: Self-evident: true without proof
senses.titleCN: 不证自明：无需论证即成立
senses.definition: true in a way that needs no argument or evidence to support it
senses.definitionCN: 真实到不需要论证或证据来支撑
senses.example: The declaration calls these truths self-evident rather than proven.
senses.exampleCN: 宣言称这些真理不证自明，而不是被证明的。
senses.why: If a fact blocks the path of doubt, no proof is needed to get around it; the road metaphor turns logical and becomes self-evidence.
senses.whyCN: 如果事实挡住了怀疑的路，就不需要证据绕行；路的比喻转为逻辑意义，成为“不证自明”。

senses.title: The obvious: a noun phrase
senses.titleCN: 显而易见的事：名词性用法
senses.definition: used as a noun in phrases such as state the obvious, meaning what everyone already knows
senses.definitionCN: 用于 state the obvious 一类短语，指人人都已知道的事
senses.example: He kept stating the obvious: that the road ahead was flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地说显而易见的事：前面的路被淹了。
senses.why: English lets an adjective stand for the thing it describes. The obvious is whatever is visible to all, and saying it aloud is the fixed phrase state the obvious.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许形容词代替它所描述的事物。the obvious 就是所有人都看得见的东西，把它说出来便成了固定短语 state the obvious。

intro.en: Obvious entered English in the 1580s from Latin obvius, literally 'in the way'. The meaning 'plain to see' is recorded from the 1630s, and the old 'commonplace' sense has died out.
intro.cn: obvious 于 16 世纪 80 年代从拉丁语 obvius 进入英语，字面是“在路上的”。“显而易见”义自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，而旧的“司空见惯”义已消亡。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'frequently met with, commonplace', a meaning that has since become obsolete.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“经常遇到、平常”，此义后来废弃。

items.en: From Latin obvius 'that is in the way, presenting itself readily, open, exposed, commonplace'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、自己送上门的、敞开的、暴露的、平常的”。

items.en: Obvius goes back to the adverb obviam 'in the way', built on ob 'in front of, against' plus viam, the accusative of via 'way'.
items.cn: obvius 出自副词 obviam“在路上”，由 ob“在前、迎着”加 viam（via“路”的宾格）构成。

items.en: Ob continues PIE *epi / *opi 'near, against'; via continues PIE *wegh- 'to go, move', the same root that gives way and wagon.
items.cn: ob 追溯到原始印欧语 *epi / *opi“近、对着”；via 追溯到 *wegh-“走、移动”，way 与 wagon 同出这个词根。

items.en: 'Plain to see, evident' is recorded from the 1630s, and this is the sense that modern English kept.
items.cn: “显而易见、明白”自 17 世纪 30 年代有记录，这正是现代英语保留的义项。

items.en: The visible branch survives in obvious, obviously and obviousness; the physical 'in the way' image survives separately in obviate and in the prefix ob-.
items.cn: “可见”这一支保留在 obvious、obviously、obviousness 中；物理性的“挡在路上”意象则另存于 obviate 和前缀 ob- 里。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to remove a difficulty or need in advance. It shares ob plus via 'way' and keeps the literal 'clear the road' image.
entries.definitionCN: 提前消除困难或需要。它同出 ob + via“路”，保留了字面的“清路”意象。

entries.definition: unaware of something happening around one. It looks close but comes from Latin oblivio 'forgetfulness', not from via.
entries.definitionCN: 对周围发生的事毫无察觉。它形似 obvious，却来自拉丁语 oblivio“遗忘”，与 via 无关。

entries.definition: feeling envy. It shares the -vious ending but goes back to Latin invidia 'envy', not to obvius.
entries.definitionCN: 嫉妒的。它同样以 -vious 结尾，但词源是拉丁语 invidia“嫉妒”，并非 obvius。

entries.definition: clear from the evidence available. It is more formal and often points to proof, while obvious points to the thing meeting the eye.
entries.definitionCN: 从已有证据看很清楚。它更正式，常指向证据；obvious 则强调事物自己撞进眼里。

entries.definition: seeming true from what is seen, which may or may not be the case. Obvious carries no such doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 从所见看来像是真的，但未必如此。obvious 不含有这层怀疑。

entries.definition: easy to see, hear or understand. It is broader and can describe sound and writing as well as sight.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或理解。它范围更广，除视觉外也能形容声音和文字。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin parts ob plus via, the via family in deviate and previous, and the fixed phrase state the obvious.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + via，deviate 与 previous 中的 via 词族，以及固定短语 state the obvious。

normal.en: ob 'in front of' plus via 'way' gives 'in the way': the thing is standing in your road, so it meets you face to face.
normal.cn: ob“在前”加 via“路”就是“在路中”：东西挡在你的路上，于是与你迎面相遇。

normal.en: via, deviate, previous and trivial all contain via 'way'; obvious is the member of the family that stands in the way.
normal.cn: via、deviate、previous、trivial 都含 via“路”；obvious 是这个词族里“挡在路上”的那一个。

normal.en: The oldest sense was 'commonplace': something met on the road every day stops being noticed.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“司空见惯”：天天在路上遇到的东西，反而不再被注意。

normal.en: State the obvious is a fixed phrase for saying what everyone can already see.
normal.cn: state the obvious 是固定短语，指把人人早已看见的事再说一遍。

normal.en: Obviously and obviousness are the everyday adverb and noun built on the same adjective.
normal.cn: obviously 和 obviousness 是由同一个形容词构成的日常副词和名词。

abstract.en: Picture a road with one boulder in the middle: you do not go looking for it, it comes to you.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路中央横着一块巨石：不是你去寻找它，而是它迎着你来。

abstract.en: The same boulder can lie on the road of thought, so a fact, a lie or a choice can all be 'in the way'.
abstract.cn: 同一块石头也能横在思维之路上，所以一个事实、一句谎话或一个选择都可以“挡在路上”。

abstract.en: When nothing blocks the road, understanding is instant; when everything is on the road, the word slides into 'commonplace'.
abstract.cn: 路上没有阻挡时，理解是瞬间的；路上全是东西时，这个词就滑向“司空见惯”。

examples.en: It was obvious from the empty shelves that the storm had caused panic buying.
examples.cn: 从空荡荡的货架一眼就能看出，风暴引发了抢购。

examples.en: She made the obvious mistake of trusting a stranger with her luggage.
examples.cn: 她犯了一个明显的错误，把行李交给了陌生人。

examples.en: The solution looks obvious only after someone has pointed it out.
examples.cn: 解决方案只有在别人指出来之后才显得显而易见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，不喂我死」——哦，不喂我就要死，这么明显的事还用说 → obvious 明显的、显而易见的

root: 源自拉丁语 obvius“挡在路上的、迎面而来的”= ob“在前、迎着”+ via“路”，核心是“横在路上、一眼撞见”；更深的 *epi / *wegh- 为原始印欧语构拟。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obvious all start from one picture: a stone standing in the middle of the road. The same obstacle then moves from the eye to the mind, to expectation, to shamelessness, and finally back to the oldest sense of 'commonplace'.
sensesIntro.cn: obvious 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一块石头立在路中央。同一个障碍随后从眼睛走到思维，走到理所当然，走到无耻，最后又回到最古老的“司空见惯”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone standing in the middle of the road, meeting you head-on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头立在路中央，迎面与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL OBSTACLE: the Latin thing that lies in the road and comes toward you.
branches.cn: 字面的障碍：拉丁语中横在路上、朝你而来的东西。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE: what stands in the open is seen at once and cannot be hidden.
branches.cn: 可见之物：摆在明处的东西一眼可见，也无从隐藏。

branches.en: THE CLEAR IDEA: the obstacle moves onto the road of thought, so understanding needs no detour or proof.
branches.cn: 清晰的想法：障碍移到思维之路上，理解不必绕道，也不必证明。

branches.en: THE ONLY OPTION AND THE BAREFACED: what is plainly visible becomes expected, and a visible fault becomes shameless.
branches.cn: 唯一选项与赤裸裸：看得见的东西变成理所当然，看得见的过失变成无耻。

branches.en: THE COMMONPLACE: what is met every day stops being noticed, and the adjective becomes the noun in the obvious.
branches.cn: 司空见惯：天天遇到的东西不再被注意；形容词也在 the obvious 中变成名词。

intro.en: Obvious is Latin ob- 'in front of, against' plus via 'way', with the adjective suffix -ous. English then adds -ly, -ness and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: obvious 由拉丁语 ob-“在前、迎着”加 via“路”，再加形容词后缀 -ous 构成。英语随后又加 -ly、-ness 和否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin obvius, from obviam 'in the way'; via 'way' is the noun at its centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 obvius，出自 obviam“在路上”；位于中心的正是名词 via“路”。

items.meaning: standing in the way, therefore plain to see
items.meaningCN: 挡在路上因而显而易见的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: The answer was obvious to the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 全班都觉得答案显而易见。

items.meaning: plainly; in a way that needs no explanation
items.meaningCN: 明显地；显然（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Obviously, the bridge is too narrow for trucks.
items.exampleCN: 显然，这座桥对卡车来说太窄了。

items.meaning: the quality of being easy to see or understand
items.meaningCN: 明显；显而易见（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: The obviousness of the error embarrassed the editor.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误如此明显，让编辑很尴尬。

items.meaning: not immediately visible or easy to understand
items.meaningCN: 不明显的；不易看出的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The link between the two events is unobvious but real.
items.exampleCN: 两件事之间的联系并不明显，但确实存在。

items.meaning: to clear a difficulty out of the way
items.example: A second entrance would obviate the need for queues.
items.exampleCN: 再开一个入口就不必排队了。

items.meaning: the act of removing a need or difficulty
items.meaningCN: 排除；预防（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The obviation of the old permit saved weeks of work.
items.exampleCN: 取消旧许可证省下了好几周的工作。

items.meaning: to move away from the road or the standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；脱离（离开原来的路）
items.example: The pilot had to deviate from the planned route.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员不得不偏离原定航线。

items.meaning: a departure from a route or standard
items.example: Any deviation from the recipe changes the taste.
items.exampleCN: 任何偏离食谱的做法都会改变味道。

items.meaning: going before on the way; earlier
items.meaningCN: 先行的；以前的（pre-“在前”+ via“路”）
items.example: The previous owner kept the keys in the shed.
items.exampleCN: 前一任房主把钥匙放在棚子里。

items.meaning: belonging to the crossroads, hence common and unimportant
items.meaningCN: 十字路口的，因而平常、不重要的
items.example: They argued over trivial details for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们为一个琐碎细节争论了一个小时。

latinEntries.meaning: in the way, open, exposed, commonplace
latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；敞开的；暴露的；平常的

latinEntries.structure: via (noun, ablative viā also used as preposition)

latinEntries.meaning: to meet, to go against, to prevent

definition_zh: 真正地；确实；真诚地；非常
definition_en: in a real or sincere way, used for emphasis, or at the end of a polite letter
core_image: 信纸最下方刚写完的一句短话，墨还没干
scene: 案头一封信写到最后一行，写的人在落款前停了停。 I am truly sorry for the trouble I caused.
sceneCN: 这里 truly 是「真诚地；真正地」（第 1 个义项：以真实、诚恳的方式）；句意为我为自己造成的麻烦真诚地道歉。信末落款前那片刻停顿，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: truly 的词根，义为「真实的」
由 true 加 -th 构成，义为「真相」
由 truth 加 -ful 构成，义为「诚实的」

senses.title: In a real way
senses.definition: in a way that is real and not merely claimed
senses.definitionCN: 以真实而非仅口头声称的方式
senses.example: I am truly sorry for the trouble I caused.
senses.exampleCN: 我为自己造成的麻烦真诚地道歉。
senses.why: The adverb takes the adjective true and adds manner: whatever is done in a true way is done truly.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词取形容词 true 并加上方式：以真实的方式去做，就是 truly 地做。

senses.title: With a sincere heart
senses.definition: with honest feeling, without pretence
senses.definitionCN: 带着真实的情感，毫不做作
senses.example: She thanked us truly, without any show.
senses.exampleCN: 她真心实意地谢我们，没有一点做作。
senses.why: The oldest sense of true was faithful, and the adverb keeps that warmth of a loyal heart.
senses.whyCN: true 最古老的意思是忠信，副词也保留了这颗忠诚之心的温度。

senses.title: As a strong emphasis
senses.definition: used before an adjective to mean really and extremely
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前表示「真的很、极其」
senses.example: The view from the ridge is truly magnificent.
senses.exampleCN: 从山脊望出去的景色确实壮丽。
senses.why: When a word must be believed strongly, truly steps in to underline it.
senses.whyCN: 当一句话需要被强烈相信时，truly 就站出来给它加下划线。

senses.title: The letter ending
senses.definition: a polite closing before a signature in a formal letter
senses.definitionCN: 正式信件署名前的礼貌结束语
senses.example: Yours truly, M. Hale.
senses.exampleCN: 您诚挚的，M. 黑尔。
senses.why: Letter writers wanted a closing that promised honesty, and this adverb offered exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 写信的人想要一句承诺诚实的结束语，这个副词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Truly is simply true plus the adverb ending -ly, with the silent e dropped in the spelling.
intro.cn: truly 就是 true 加上副词词尾 -ly，拼写时去掉了不发音的 e。

items.en: The root treuwaz meant firm and loyal, the seed of both true and truth.
items.cn: 词根 treuwaz 意为牢固、忠实，是 true 与 truth 的种子。

items.en: Old English had treowlice, meaning faithfully, already with the adverb ending.
items.cn: 古英语已有 treowlice，意为忠实地，当时就带着副词词尾。

items.en: The form settled as truly after the e was dropped before the suffix.
items.cn: 在词尾前去 e 之后，拼写固定为 truly。

items.en: The adverb grew into an intensifier, as in truly wonderful.
items.cn: 这个副词发展出强调用法，如 truly wonderful。

items.en: Yours truly became a standard closing in letters and later a joking name for oneself.
items.cn: Yours truly 成了信件的标准结束语，后来又成了自称的戏谑说法。

note.en: The first group shares the tru stem, the second holds other adverbs of truth and sincerity.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tru 词干，第二组收其他表示真实与诚恳的副词。

entries.definition: Agreeing with the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的

entries.definition: That which agrees with the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 真相；真理

entries.definition: In an honest way.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实地

entries.definition: In fact, or used for emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；确实

entries.definition: With honest feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 真诚地

entries.definition: In a real and true manner.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；由衷地

normalIntro.en: Remember the spelling: truly has no e, though true does.
normalIntro.cn: 记住拼写：truly 里没有 e，而 true 里有。

normal.en: Drop the e before -ly: true becomes truly.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 前去 e：true 变 truly。

normal.en: Yours truly signs the end of a formal letter.
normal.cn: Yours truly 用在正式信件末尾署名。

normal.en: Truly before an adjective simply means very.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前，truly 就是「非常」。

normal.en: The word keeps the old sense of faithful.
normal.cn: 这个词保留忠实的古义。

normal.en: It is often used with sorry and grateful.
normal.cn: 它常与 sorry、grateful 连用。

abstract.en: A pen resting on the last line of a letter.
abstract.cn: 搁在信末一行上的笔。

abstract.en: A voice without any acting in it.
abstract.cn: 一个不带任何表演的声音。

abstract.en: A word underlined twice on a page.
abstract.cn: 纸上被划了两道线的词。

examples.en: I truly believe she meant no harm.
examples.cn: 我确实相信她并无恶意。

examples.en: It was a truly beautiful morning after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后是一个真正美丽的清晨。

examples.en: He said he was grateful, and he meant it sincerely.
examples.cn: 他说他很感激，而且说得真心实意。

dict_mnemonic.text: true＋ly，去掉 e——老老实实地做一件事，就是真正地、真诚地。

root: 由 true（古英语 treowe，忠信、牢固）加副词词尾 -ly 构成，古英语已有 treowlice；同族词有 true、truth、truthful。

sensesIntro.en: Real manner first, then sincere feeling, then emphasis, then the closing of a letter.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是真实的方式，再是诚恳的心意，然后是强调，最后是信末的结束语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen on the last line of a letter.
core.cn: 核心意象：信末那行上的笔。

branches.en: The reality branch: done in a real way.
branches.cn: 真实分支：以真实的方式做到。

branches.en: The sincerity branch: feeling without pretence.
branches.cn: 诚恳分支：没有做作的情感。

branches.en: The emphasis branch: underlining a word.
branches.cn: 强调分支：给一个词加下划线。

branches.en: The letter branch: a promise of honesty before a name.
branches.cn: 信件分支：名字之前的一句诚实承诺。

branches.en: The tone branch: both speak to a reader with respect.
branches.cn: 语气分支：两者都以敬意对读者说话。

intro.en: Truly is the stem tru plus the adverb ending -ly, a very common English pattern.
intro.cn: truly 是词干 tru 加副词词尾 -ly，这是英语中最常见的构词模式之一。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but the adverb ending itself came into English through Latin models.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自日耳曼语，但副词词尾本身是借拉丁语范式进入英语的。

items.example: The stem is the adjective without its final e.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干就是去掉末尾 e 的形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb.
The old root of firmness survives here.

definition_zh: 至关重要的；决定性的
definition_en: extremely important because everything else depends on it
core_image: 一座窄桥只容一人通过，桥下是深谷
scene: 队伍走到一座窄桥前，桥下是深谷。 One wrong step would be crucial for the whole climb.
sceneCN: 这里 crucial 指「至关重要的」（第 1 个义项：整个结果都取决于它的）；句意是走错一步，对整次攀登都至关重要。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: so important that the whole outcome depends on it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到整个结果都取决于它
senses.example: Sleep is crucial for memory.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对记忆至关重要。
senses.why: One thing can hold up everything that comes after it.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西，就能撑住它之后的全部。

senses.title: Decisive at a turning point
senses.definition: settling the result at one particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个特定时刻把结果定下来
senses.example: That vote was crucial to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那次投票对这项计划是决定性的。
senses.why: Where two roads part, one step decides the rest.
senses.whyCN: 两条路分岔的地方，一步就定下余下的路。

intro.en: Crucial comes from Latin crux, a cross, through Medieval Latin crucialis.
intro.cn: crucial 源自拉丁语 crux（十字），经中世纪拉丁语 crucialis 而来。

items.en: Crux meant a cross, where two lines met.
items.cn: crux 指十字，是两条线相交之处。

items.en: Crucialis meant belonging to a cross.
items.cn: crucialis 意为与十字有关的。

items.en: A crossroad forced a traveller to choose.
items.cn: 十字路口迫使行人做出选择。

items.en: Crucial first meant shaped like a cross.
items.cn: crucial 最初意为十字形的。

items.en: It took the sense of decisive, like a crossroad.
items.cn: 它取得如十字路口般「决定性」的意思。

items.en: It now simply means extremely important.
items.cn: 今天它只表示极其重要。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cruc- stem, and the meaning group names other words for what decides an outcome.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cruc- 词干，近义组列出其他表示决定成败的说法。

entries.definition: a mark or shape of two lines
entries.definitionCN: 两条线构成的记号或形状

entries.definition: the central point of a problem
entries.definitionCN: 问题的核心所在

entries.definition: in a way that decides everything
entries.definitionCN: 以决定一切的方式

entries.definition: so important that the result depends on it
entries.definitionCN: 重要到结果取决于它

entries.definition: necessary for life or success
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的

entries.definition: settling a result completely
entries.definitionCN: 彻底定下结果的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a narrow bridge and end at a crossroad with no sign.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一座窄桥开始，最后落到一个没有路牌的十字路口。

normal.en: Crucial hides a cross: a place where you must choose.
normal.cn: crucial 里藏着一个十字：那是你必须选的地方。

normal.en: One step on a narrow bridge decides the climb.
normal.cn: 窄桥上的第一步，定下整次攀登。

normal.en: Not everything matters; one thing matters most.
normal.cn: 不是一切都重要，只有一样最重要。

normal.en: At a crossroad, both roads look the same in the dark.
normal.cn: 在十字路口，黑暗里两条路看起来一模一样。

normal.en: Say crucial when the whole plan hangs on it.
normal.cn: 整个计划都挂在上面时，就说至关重要。

abstract.en: Picture a plank over a deep gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板横在深沟上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a rail, holding steady.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶住栏杆，稳住不动。

abstract.en: Picture two roads splitting with no sign.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路分开，却没有路牌。

examples.en: Clean water is crucial to public health.
examples.cn: 清洁的水对公共健康至关重要。

examples.en: The next ten minutes were crucial.
examples.cn: 接下来的十分钟是决定性的。

examples.en: Trust plays a crucial role in any team.
examples.cn: 信任在任何团队里都起关键作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crucial 记成一个十字路口：往左往右全看这一步，所以它至关重要。

root: 源自拉丁语 crux（十字）与中世纪拉丁语 crucialis；本义是「十字形的」，因十字路口必须做出抉择，19 世纪起引申为决定性的、至关重要的。

sensesIntro.en: From the weight of one thing, to the moment that settles the rest.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一样东西的分量，到把余下一切定下来的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow bridge over a deep gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在深沟上的一座窄桥。

branches.en: One factor carries the weight of all the others.
branches.cn: 一个因素，扛着其余全部因素的分量。

branches.en: At a crossroad, a single step settles the direction.
branches.cn: 在十字路口，一步就定下方向。

branches.en: What is decisive is decisive because it is needed.
branches.cn: 决定性的东西之所以决定性，是因为它被需要。

branches.en: Remove it, and the whole plan falls.
branches.cn: 把它抽走，整个计划就塌了。

branches.en: The moment is small, but everything hangs on it.
branches.cn: 那一刻很小，可一切都挂在它上面。

intro.en: Crucial is built on the Latin crux, a cross, with the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: crucial 建在拉丁语 crux（十字）之上，加了形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crux also gives cross, crux and crusade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux 还生出 cross、crux 与 crusade。

items.meaning: in a way that decides the result
items.example: Crucially, the door was left open.
The report stressed the cruciality of water.
items.exampleCN: 报告强调了水的重要性。
一个十字标出了那个地点。

items.meaning: the central point of a problem
items.example: That is the crux of the matter.
She led a crusade for clean air.
items.exampleCN: 她发起了一场争取清洁空气的运动。

items.example: The church has a cruciform plan.
items.exampleCN: 这座教堂是十字形平面。

items.meaning: to put to death on a cross
items.example: The story says he was crucified.
items.exampleCN: 故事说他被钉上了十字架。

latinEntries.example: Latin crux named the crossing point.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 crux 指相交之处。

definition_zh: 选择；选项；选择权；（金融）期权；（计算机）选项
definition_en: one of several things that can be chosen; the freedom or right to choose; a right to buy or sell something at a fixed price
core_image: 几张摊开的牌，你伸手只拿起其中一张
scene: 申请研究生时，她在纸上列出三所学校，比较学费、城市和专业方向。 She wrote: Each school is one option, and I can keep all three open until the last week.
sceneCN: 这里 option 是「可供选择的方案」（第 1 个义项：可选的事物之一）；句意：每一所学校都是一个选项，我可以把这三所学校都留到最后一刻再决定。图中可辨识物件：申请表、三所学校名单、铅笔、计算器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 选择；选项；可选择的事物

collocations.zh: 保留选择余地；不急于定死

senses.title: One of the things you can choose
senses.definition: one of two or more things that you can choose to have or do
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可供选择的事物中的一个
senses.example: Studying abroad is one option; staying at home is another.
senses.exampleCN: 出国留学是一种选择，留在国内是另一种选择。
senses.why: The word names the item sitting in front of the chooser. Latin optio meant 'choice' as an act; by 1885 English extended it to 'the thing that may be chosen', so the abstract act became a concrete item on a list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指“选择”这个行为，后来指摆在选择者面前的那一项。拉丁语 optio 是“选择”；英语到 1885 年才把它扩展到“可供选择的事物”，抽象行为于是变成了清单上的具体一项。

senses.title: The freedom or right to choose
senses.definition: the power or liberty of choosing, especially when nothing is forced
senses.definitionCN: 选择的能力或自由，尤指没有被强迫时
senses.example: Employees have the option of working from home two days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以选择每周有两天在家办公。
senses.why: From c. 1600 'action of choosing' came the 1630s sense 'power or liberty of choosing'. The emphasis moves from the chosen item to the chooser's open hand: what matters is that the hand is not forced.
senses.whyCN: 从 1600 年前后的“选择行为”，发展出 1630 年代的“选择权、选择自由”。重点从被选的物件移到了选择者那只未被强迫的手。

senses.title: An extra feature you may add
senses.titleCN: 可选配置：加钱才有的附加功能
senses.definition: a feature or piece of equipment that is available only if the buyer chooses and usually pays for it
senses.definitionCN: 只有买家选择并通常额外付费才提供的功能或设备
senses.example: Air conditioning is an option on this model, not standard equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 空调是这款车型的选装配置，不是标配。
senses.why: Here the choice itself is turned into a product. The buyer's open hand is priced: you may take the extra feature or leave it, and either way the base item still works.
senses.whyCN: 这里被出售的正是“选择”本身。选择者那只张开的手被标上了价格：你可以拿这项附加功能，也可以不拿，而基础产品照样能用。

senses.title: Stock option: a right to buy shares
senses.titleCN: 股票期权：按约定价格买股份的权利
senses.definition: a right given to an employee or investor to buy company shares at a set price within a set period
senses.definitionCN: 给予员工或投资者在约定期限内按约定价格购买公司股份的权利
senses.example: The startup offered her stock options as part of the package.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司把股票期权作为薪酬方案的一部分提供给她。
senses.why: A share option is literally a purchased choice: the holder may buy at the fixed price or walk away. The 1755 commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium' is the direct ancestor of this financial use.
senses.whyCN: 股票期权字面上就是“买来的选择权”：持有人可以按固定价格买入，也可以放弃。1755 年那条“支付权利金换得的特权”的商业义，正是这一金融用法的直系祖先。

senses.title: Option contract: a right with a price
senses.titleCN: 期权合约：有价格的权利
senses.definition: a contract giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a stated price before a deadline
senses.definitionCN: 赋予买方在截止日期前按约定价格买入或卖出资产的权利而非义务的合约
senses.example: The fund bought an option to purchase the land at a fixed price.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金买入了按固定价格购买这块土地的选择权。
senses.why: The legal instrument isolates the core idea of the word: a choice that is bought, bounded by a price and a date. The holder pays for the open hand and may still refuse to close it.
senses.whyCN: 这种法律工具把词的核心抽离出来：一个被买下、受价格和日期约束的选择。持有人为那只张开的手付费，并且仍然可以拒绝合拢。

senses.title: The option play in football
senses.titleCN: 美式橄榄球中的“选择战术”
senses.definition: an American football play in which the ball carrier may either pass or run
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中持球者可选择传球或自己带球推进的战术
senses.example: The quarterback kept the ball on the option play.
senses.exampleCN: 四分卫在这个选择战术中自己带球推进。
senses.why: Recorded by 1953, the play gives the carrier two live choices at the moment of action. The name is not about a product or a contract but about a decision still open while the body is already moving.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法记录于 1953 年：战术让持球者在动作发生的瞬间保有两条真实可走的路线。名字说的不是产品或合约，而是身体已经动起来时仍然敞开的选择。

senses.title: A setting or flag in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的选项或参数开关
senses.definition: a selectable setting, flag, or argument that changes how a program behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变程序行为方式的可选设置、开关或参数
senses.example: Add the -v option to see verbose output.
senses.exampleCN: 加上 -v 选项即可查看详细输出。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the everyday sense: a program offers a menu of behaviours, and the user picks one. The choice is now made by typing a flag rather than by pointing at a card.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了日常义：程序把若干行为列成菜单，用户挑一个。选择方式从“指着卡片”变成了“敲一个参数”。

senses.title: Keeping alternatives available
senses.titleCN: 保留余地：让选择继续敞开
senses.definition: in the phrase keep options open, to avoid committing so that alternatives stay available
senses.definitionCN: 用于 keep options open，表示不做出承诺，以便保留其他可能
senses.example: She kept her options open by applying to several programs.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了好几个项目，以此保留选择余地。
