senses.why: This phrase makes the open hand visible. Not choosing yet is itself a choice, because the alternatives remain graspable and no single card has been lifted from the table.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让“张开的手”变得可见。暂不选择本身也是一种选择：其他可能仍然可抓，桌上没有哪张牌被真正拿走。

intro.en: Option comes from Latin through French. The date of the English noun is clear; the origin of the Latin verb optare is not, and standard references mark it as uncertain.
intro.cn: option 经由法语来自拉丁语。英语名词的年代清楚，但拉丁动词 optare 的来源并不清楚，通行资料标注为不确定。

items.en: c. 1600, 'action of choosing'; by the 1630s, 'power or liberty of choosing'. The noun entered English through French option (Old French opcion).
items.cn: 约 1600 年记录为“选择的行为”；到 1630 年代为“选择的能力或自由”。名词经法语 option（古法语 opcion）进入英语。

items.en: From Latin optionem (nominative optio) 'choice, free choice, liberty to choose', a noun from optare 'to desire, pray for, choose'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 optionem（主格 optio）“选择、自由选择、选择的自由”，是由 optare“渴望、祈求、选择”构成的名词。

items.en: De Vaan derives optare from Proto-Italic *opeje- 'to choose, grab', from PIE *hopeie-, and compares Hittite epp-/app- 'to take, grab'. This deeper reconstruction is debated, so the ultimate root is source uncertain.
items.cn: De Vaan 把 optare 追溯到原始意大利语 *opeje-“选择、抓取”，再往上到原始印欧语 *hopeie-，并与赫梯语 epp-/app-“拿、抓”比较。这一更深层重构仍有争议，故最底层词源来源不确定。

items.en: 1755 records the commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium'; 1885 records 'thing that may be chosen'. The word thus moved from act to right to object.
items.cn: 1755 年记录商业义“支付权利金换得的特权”；1885 年记录“可供选择的事物”。词义由此从行为走到权利，再走到物件。

items.en: 1953 records the football option play. The computing sense of a selectable flag is a later 20c. extension of the everyday 'choice' meaning.
items.cn: 1953 年记录橄榄球的 option play（选择战术）。计算机中“可选开关”的义项是 20 世纪后期由日常“选择”义扩展而来。

note.en: The first group separates words that merely look like option; the second compares words that really mean a choice.
note.cn: 第一组只把外形相近的词分开；第二组比较真正表示“选择”的词。

entries.definition: a process or set of actions, especially in surgery or business. It starts with op- but comes from Latin opus 'work', not optare.
entries.definitionCN: 操作；手术；业务。它同样以 op- 开头，但来自拉丁语 opus“工作”，而不是 optare。

entries.definition: a belief or judgment not fully proved. It is linked in dictionaries to opinari 'to think', whose own origin is unknown, and is not a form of option.
entries.definitionCN: 意见；看法。词典把它连到 opinari“认为”，而 opinari 本身来源不明，它不是 option 的变形。

entries.definition: relating to light or the eyes. Its opt- goes back to Greek optos 'seen', a different root from Latin optare.
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；视觉的。它的 opt- 来自希腊语 optos“被看见的”，与拉丁语 optare 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: in grammar, a mood that expresses a wish. It is built directly on Latin optare 'to wish', so it is a true relative of option.
entries.definitionCN: 语法中的祈愿语气。它直接由拉丁语 optare“希望”构成，因此是 option 的真正同族词。

entries.definition: the act of choosing, or the range of things from which one may choose. It is the everyday word; option is more formal and often implies a listed alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 选择的行为，或可供选择的整体范围。它是最日常的词；option 更正式，常指清单上列出的一个备选。

entries.definition: one of two or more possibilities that can replace each other. It stresses replacement; option stresses that the thing is available to pick.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个可相互替代的可能之一。它强调“替换”，option 强调“可供挑选”。

entries.definition: the act of selecting, or the set of things chosen. It often refers to a curated range rather than a single item.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的行为，或被挑出的一组事物。它常指经过整理的一组，而不是单个选项。

entries.definition: a stronger liking for one thing over another. It names the ranking in the chooser's mind, not the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物更强的偏好。它指选择者心里的排序，而不是被选的那个事物。

normalIntro.en: Five sound-and-spelling hooks, then three abstract images for the idea behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住这个词背后的观念。

normal.en: op- sounds like 'open': an option is a door left open until you walk through one.
normal.cn: op- 听起来像 open（打开）：option 就是一扇直到你走进某一间之前都开着的门。

normal.en: -tion marks an action, as in action: choosing is something you do, not a thing that happens to you.
normal.cn: -tion 像 action 里的那个 -tion，标记“动作”：选择是你做的事，不是落到你身上的事。

normal.en: opt out is 'choose out', opt in is 'choose in': the same root with opposite directions.
normal.cn: opt out 是“选出去”（退出），opt in 是“选进来”（加入）：同一个词根，方向相反。

normal.en: Keep options open = keep the cards on the table, not in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep options open＝把牌留在桌上，而不是揣进口袋。

normal.en: optional ends in -al like 'additional': an optional extra is one you may add.
normal.cn: optional 和 additional 一样以 -al 结尾：optional extra 就是你可以“加”的那一项。

abstract.en: An option is the smallest unit of freedom: a real alternative that you can still take.
abstract.cn: 选项是自由的最小单位：一个你仍然拿得走的真实备选。

abstract.en: Every option is a road not yet walked; choosing burns the other roads for this trip.
abstract.cn: 每个选项都是一条尚未走过的路；一旦选择，这一趟的其他路就被烧掉了。

abstract.en: A financial option puts a price on possibility itself: you pay to keep a choice alive.
abstract.cn: 金融期权给“可能性”本身标了价：你付钱，只为让一个选择继续活着。

examples.en: The report lists several options for cutting costs, but none is painless.
examples.cn: 报告列出了几种削减成本的选项，但没有一种是轻松的。

examples.en: You always have the option to say no.
examples.cn: 你始终拥有拒绝的选项。

examples.en: The software hides advanced options unless you open the settings panel.
examples.cn: 除非打开设置面板，否则软件会隐藏高级选项。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 opt- 记成“伸手抓取”，-ion 记成“动作”：抓取的动作就是选择。
dict_mnemonic.text: opt（抓取、选择）+ -ion（名词）→ 选择、选项、选择权

root: 拉丁 optare“希望、选择”→ optio“选择”→ 法语 option → 英语 option；更早的原始印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from 'a thing you may pick' to 'the right to pick', then to priced choices (features, stock, contracts), and finally to a live choice inside a game, a program, or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“可供挑选的事物”走到“挑选的权利”，再到被标价的选择（选装配置、股票、合约），最后落到比赛、程序与计划中仍然敞开的那一次选择。

core.en: An open hand above several alternatives, ready to lift one
core.cn: 悬在几个备选之上的手，随时准备拿起一个

branches.en: Concrete alternatives: one item on a list of things you may pick.
branches.cn: 具体备选：可供挑选的清单上的一项。

branches.en: Freedom kept open: the chooser's liberty, or the deliberate refusal to commit.
branches.cn: 被保留的自由：选择者的权利，或有意不作承诺。

branches.en: Choices sold as goods: an add-on feature or a stock option.
branches.cn: 作为商品出售的选择：选装配置或股票期权。

branches.en: Choices inside a system: a football play or a software flag.
branches.cn: 系统内部的选择：橄榄球战术或软件开关。

branches.en: The paid right: liberty turned into a priced, time-limited contract.
branches.cn: 付费的权利：自由变成有价格、有期限的合约。

intro.en: The opt- family is small but busy: a verb of choosing, a noun of choice, and adjectives that mark whether something is left to the chooser.
intro.cn: opt- 词族不大但很活跃：一个“选择”动词、一个“选择”名词，以及标记“是否交由选择者决定”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare 'to wish, choose' yields optio 'choice' and the adjective optativus 'expressing a wish'. English opt is a back-formation from option.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare“希望、选择”产生 optio“选择”和形容词 optativus“表达愿望的”。英语的 opt 是从 option 逆构出来的动词。

items.meaning: the act or right of choosing; a thing chosen
items.meaningCN: 选择的行为或权利；被选中的事物
items.example: You have the option to decline.

items.meaning: in a way that is not required
items.example: The form can optionally include a photo.
items.exampleCN: 表格可以选择附上一张照片。

items.meaning: to choose or decide between alternatives
items.example: Most students opt for the shorter course.
items.exampleCN: 大多数学生选择较短的那门课。

items.meaning: a choice to leave or not take part
items.example: The newsletter uses an opt-out system.
items.exampleCN: 这份通讯采用“默认订阅、可退出”的机制。

items.meaning: a choice to join or take part
items.exampleCN: 营销邮件需要用户主动选择加入的同意。

items.meaning: to choose for oneself and take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 采纳；收养（选择过来成为自己的）
items.example: The school adopted a new reading method.
items.exampleCN: 学校采纳了一种新的阅读教学法。

items.meaning: the act of taking something as one's own
items.example: The adoption of the plan took two years.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划的采纳用了两年。

items.meaning: expressing a wish, as a grammatical mood
items.example: Ancient Greek has an optative mood.

latinEntries.example: Latin optare aliquid means to wish for something.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 optare aliquid 意为“渴望某物”。

latinEntries.meaning: choice, free choice, liberty to choose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 选择、自由选择、选择的自由
latinEntries.example: Optio is the source of French option.
latinEntries.exampleCN: optio 是法语 option 的来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to choose for oneself, take by choice
latinEntries.meaningCN: 为自己挑选；选择并接纳
latinEntries.example: Adoptare is the source of English adopt.
latinEntries.exampleCN: adoptare 是英语 adopt 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Optativus modus is the wishing mood.

definition_zh: 许多的；数量众多的；为数不少的
definition_en: existing in large numbers; many in count
core_image: 沙滩上一眼数不完的贝壳一直铺到浪线尽头
scene: 广场上一队接一队的人来登记，志愿者手里的表格翻了一页又一页。 Numerous volunteers signed up before noon.
sceneCN: 这里指人数众多（第 2 个义项：人数很多的一群人）；句意为中午之前就有许多志愿者报名；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A large number of things
senses.definition: a large number of separate countable things
senses.definitionCN: 可单独计数的事物数量很大
senses.example: The shelf holds numerous small boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上放着许多小盒子。
senses.why: Latin numerus meant number and count, and the suffix -osus means full of, so numerous is literally full of number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 numerus 意为数目与计数，后缀 -osus 意为充满，因此 numerous 字面就是「充满数目」。

senses.title: A great many people
senses.definition: a large body of people
senses.definitionCN: 人数很多的一群人
senses.example: Numerous guests arrived before the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 许多客人在仪式开始前就到了。
senses.why: The adjective is at home with crowds because Latin numerosus described troops as well as things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与人群天然相合，因为拉丁 numerosus 既描述事物，也描述军队。

senses.title: Many separate occasions
senses.definition: happening on many separate occasions over time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上分属许多不同场合
senses.example: She raised the point on numerous occasions.
senses.exampleCN: 她在许多场合提出过这一点。
senses.why: Counting moves from objects to events, and the word follows without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 计数从物件转到事件，这个词的形态不变地跟了过去。

senses.title: Many items spread over an area
senses.titleCN: 散布在广大区域内的许多事物
senses.definition: many separate items scattered across a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 许多独立事物散布在广阔区域内
senses.example: The delta contains numerous islands.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲上有众多岛屿。
senses.why: A map shows the count as spread, and the same adjective covers that view.
senses.whyCN: 地图把数量呈现为散落状态，同一个形容词也能覆盖这种视角。

senses.title: Many supporting details
senses.definition: supplied in great quantity, as notes or examples
senses.definitionCN: 以大量注释或例证的形式提供
senses.example: The paper offers numerous examples of the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文为这一模式提供了大量例证。
senses.why: In academic prose the word counts evidence rather than objects.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作中，这个词数的是证据，而不是物件。

senses.title: Many reasons in an argument
senses.definition: many points offered in support of a claim
senses.definitionCN: 为支持某一主张而提出的许多论点
senses.example: There are numerous reasons to postpone the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 推迟投票的理由有很多。
senses.why: Debate turns quantity into weight, and the adjective supplies the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 辩论把数量变成分量，这个形容词负责提供数量。

senses.title: A large sample in research
senses.definition: a large count of cases in a study or survey
senses.definitionCN: 研究或调查中大量案例的计数
senses.example: Numerous trials confirmed the effect.
senses.exampleCN: 大量试验确认了这一效应。
senses.why: Statistics needs a plain word for a big count before any test is run.
senses.whyCN: 统计在运行任何检验之前，需要一个表示大计数的平实词。

senses.title: A formal substitute for many
senses.definition: used in formal writing where a bare many would sound abrupt
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式写作，替下显得突兀的「许多」
senses.example: Numerous factors were considered by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会考虑了诸多因素。
senses.why: Register, not meaning, separates numerous from many in much modern use.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法中，这个词与「许多」的区别多在语体，而非意义。

intro.en: Numerous is Latin numerosus, full of number, built on numerus plus the suffix -osus. The Latin line is clear; the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: numerous 来自拉丁 numerosus「充满数目」，由 numerus 加后缀 -osus 构成。拉丁线索清楚，英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, and also a rank or division; its deeper origin is usually traced to a root meaning to assign or allot.
items.cn: numerus 指数目、计数，也指等级或队列；更深的来源通常追到一个表示「分配」的词根。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of or abounding in, so numerosus is literally full of number.
items.cn: 后缀 -osus 意为充满、多有，因此 numerosus 字面就是「充满数目」。

items.en: The adjective described things countable in great quantity, especially troops, examples and occasions.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述可大量计数之物，尤用于军队、例证与场合。

items.en: English took the adjective in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word survives mainly in formal writing as a polished substitute for many.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在正式写作中，作为 many 的雅致替身。

items.en: Number, numeral, enumerate and numerator all descend from numerus, while numerous is its adjective.
items.cn: number、numeral、enumerate 与 numerator 都出自 numerus，numerous 则是它的形容词。

note.en: The first group descends from the Latin number word; the second group gives plainer ways of saying a large count.
note.cn: 第一组出自拉丁语「数目」一词；第二组是表示「大量」的更平实说法。

entries.definition: A count or total, reaching English through French from Latin numerus.
entries.definitionCN: 计数或总数，经法语从拉丁 numerus 进入英语。

entries.definition: A sign or word for a number.
entries.definitionCN: 表示数目的符号或词。

entries.definition: Expressed in or relating to numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字表示的；与数字有关的。

entries.definition: To list items one by one, from the same number stem.
entries.definitionCN: 逐项列举，出自同一「数目」词干。

entries.definition: Able to be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 可以计数的。

entries.definition: A large but unspecified number; plainer than numerous.
entries.definitionCN: 数量大而未指明；比 numerous 更平实。

entries.definition: Too many to count.
entries.definitionCN: 多到数不清。

entries.definition: Present in great quantity, often of supply rather than items.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在，多指供给而非条目。

entries.definition: A countless or extremely great number, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 无数或极多，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: More than two but not a large number.
entries.definitionCN: 多于两个，但数量不算大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin number word, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「数目」词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Numerus is number, and -osus means full of, so numerous means full of numbers.
normal.cn: numerus 是数目，-osus 意为充满，所以 numerous 就是「满是数目」。

normal.en: Number, numeral, enumerate and numerator all come from the same stem.
normal.cn: number、numeral、enumerate 与 numerator 都出自同一词干。

normal.en: The fixed phrase for many occasions marks the time sense.
normal.cn: 表示「在许多场合」的固定说法标出时间义。

normal.en: Numerous replaces many most often in formal writing.
normal.cn: numerous 多在正式写作中替下「许多」这一平实说法。

normal.en: A large sample is described as numerous trials or numerous cases.
normal.cn: 大样本常被说成「大量试验」或「大量案例」。

abstract.en: Numerous is a beach where the shells outnumber the footprints.
abstract.cn: 「众多」是一片沙滩，贝壳比脚印还多。

abstract.en: A count becomes a crowd, and a crowd becomes a weight in an argument.
abstract.cn: 计数变成人群，人群又变成论证里的分量。

abstract.en: The word never says exactly how many, only that counting would take a while.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不说确切多少，只说数起来要花些时间。

examples.en: Numerous small faults appeared along the surface of the beam.
examples.cn: 梁的表面出现了许多细小裂纹。

examples.en: The archive holds numerous letters from the same household.
examples.cn: 档案馆存有这一户人家的许多信件。

examples.en: Numerous attempts failed before the method was found.
examples.cn: 在找到方法之前，已有许多次尝试失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「牛魔若死」——牛魔王的兵多到数不清：众多的

root: 拉丁 numerosus「充满数目的」← numerus「数目、计数」+ -osus「充满」；numerus 更深来源一般认为与「分配」有关。同族 number、numeral、enumerate、numerator 均出 numerus，而 numerous 是该词的形容词。英语十六世纪借入，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses count from objects to people, occasions, places, evidence, reasons, samples, and finally to formal register.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从物件数到人、场合、地域、证据、理由、样本，最后落到正式语体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shells on a beach, more than anyone could finish counting before the tide turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙滩上的贝壳，多到潮水转向之前谁也数不完。

branches.en: THE COUNT ITSELF: items large in number, whether stacked or scattered.
branches.cn: 计数本身：数量很大的事物，无论堆叠还是散落。

branches.en: THE CROWD: a large body of people.
branches.cn: 人群：人数很多的一群人。

branches.en: THE REPEATED CASE: many occasions and a large sample of trials.
branches.cn: 重复的个案：许多场合与大量试验样本。

branches.en: THE SUPPORTING MATERIAL: many examples and many reasons offered together.
branches.cn: 支撑材料：一起给出的许多例证与许多理由。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: the formal stand-in for a bare many.
branches.cn: 语体：用于正式写作、替下 many 的说法。

intro.en: Numerous is Latin numerosus plus the English adjective ending; the stem is the Latin number word.
intro.cn: numerous 是拉丁 numerosus 加英语形容词词尾；词干就是拉丁语「数目」一词。

latinIntro.en: Numerus gives the noun family, -osus turns it into full of, and English keeps the adjective beside number and numeral.
latinIntro.cn: numerus 提供名词词族，-osus 把它变成「充满」，英语则让这个形容词与 number、numeral 并存。

items.example: The stem names the act of counting.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名计数的行为。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into plenty.
Latin already used the adjective for troops and examples.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语已用它形容军队与例证。

items.example: French carried numerus across the Channel as nombre.
items.exampleCN: 法语把 numerus 以 nombre 的形式带过海峡。

items.example: The family separates the sign from the count.
items.exampleCN: 词族把符号与计数分开。

items.example: The verb walks through the items in order.
items.exampleCN: 动词按顺序把条目走一遍。

items.example: English shortened the Latin ending to -ous.
The adverb is rare but regular.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词罕见但构词规则。

items.example: It also builds famous, dangerous and anxious.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 famous、dangerous 与 anxious。

items.meaning: the top term of a fraction
items.example: The counter of parts keeps the number stem.
items.exampleCN: 分数的「计数者」保留了数目词干。

definition_zh: 当代的；同时代的；同时代的人
definition_en: belonging to the present time, or existing at the same time as something else
core_image: 一间摆着现代家具和旧木梁的屋子，两个时代并排
scene: 美术馆的一层正在展出当下艺术家的作品。 The museum has a whole floor of contemporary art.
sceneCN: 这里 contemporary 指「当代的」（第 1 个义项：属于当下这个时代）；句意是这家美术馆有整整一层当代艺术。

senses.title: Of the present age
senses.definition: belonging to the time we live in now
senses.definitionCN: 属于我们现在生活的这个时代
senses.example: She collects contemporary paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 她收藏当代绘画。
senses.why: Every age calls itself the present, and means it.
senses.whyCN: 每个时代都把自己叫作当下，而且说得很真诚。

senses.title: Of the same time
senses.definition: existing or happening in the same period as something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物存在于同一个时期
senses.example: These two buildings are contemporary with each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座建筑属于同一时代。
senses.why: Two things can share a century without ever meeting.
senses.whyCN: 两件事可以共处一个世纪，却从未相遇。

senses.title: A person of the same age
senses.definition: a person who lived or worked at the same time as another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人同时生活或工作的人
senses.example: He was a contemporary of the young Mozart.
senses.exampleCN: 他是青年莫扎特的同时代人。
senses.why: History is easier to see beside someone who stood next to it.
senses.whyCN: 历史若挨着一个曾站在旁边的人来看，会清楚些。

intro.en: Contemporary comes from Latin contemporarius, built from com-, together, and tempus, time.
intro.cn: contemporary 来自拉丁语 contemporarius，由 com-（一起）与 tempus（时间）构成。

items.en: Tempus meant time or a period of time.
items.cn: tempus 意为时间或一段时期。

items.en: Contemporarius meant sharing the same time.
items.cn: contemporarius 意为共处同一时间。

items.en: It described events and people of one period.
items.cn: 它用来描述同一时期的事件与人物。

items.en: French contemporain carried both the present and the same-time senses.
items.cn: 法语 contemporain 同时带有当下与同时两层意思。

items.en: English contemporary first meant living at the same time.
items.cn: 英语 contemporary 最初指生活在同一时期。

items.en: It now usually points to art and culture of our own day.
items.cn: 如今它通常指我们这一天的艺术与文化。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin time base tempor-, and the meaning group names other words for what belongs to now.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语时间词基 tempor-，近义组列出其他表示「属于现在」的词。

entries.definition: lasting only for a short time
entries.definitionCN: 临时的；短暂的

entries.definition: happening in the same period
entries.definitionCN: 同时代的；同时发生的

entries.definition: the speed at which music is played
entries.definitionCN: 速度；节拍

entries.definition: relating to the present or recent times
entries.definitionCN: 现代的；近代的

entries.definition: happening or existing now
entries.definitionCN: 当前的；现行的

entries.definition: existing at this moment
entries.definitionCN: 现在的；目前的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a room where new chairs stand under old beams, then move to two lives sharing one century.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从新椅子摆在旧木梁下的房间开始，再到共享一个世纪的两个人。

normal.en: Con- is together and tempor is time, so contemporary is sharing one time.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tempor 是时间，contemporary 就是共处同一时间。

normal.en: Contemporary art is the art of the room you are standing in.
normal.cn: 当代艺术，就是你此刻站着的那间屋子里的艺术。

normal.en: Two painters of one year are contemporaries, even if they never met.
normal.cn: 同一年份的两位画家就是同时代人，哪怕从未见过。

normal.en: Temporary lasts a while; contemporary means this while.
normal.cn: temporary 是持续一阵子，contemporary 指的是眼下这一阵。

normal.en: Every era thinks it is the final one.
normal.cn: 每个时代都以为自己是最后一个。

abstract.en: Picture old wooden beams above a clean new table.
abstract.cn: 想象旧木梁下面一张干净的新桌子。

abstract.en: Picture two calendars hanging side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象两本日历并排挂着。

abstract.en: Picture a gallery wall lit by a single lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象画廊的一面墙被一盏灯照亮。

examples.en: The gallery shows contemporary Chinese painting.
examples.cn: 这家画廊展出中国当代绘画。

examples.en: The poet was a contemporary of Shakespeare.
examples.cn: 这位诗人是莎士比亚的同时代人。

examples.en: Contemporary life moves faster than it did a century ago.
examples.cn: 当代生活比一个世纪前快得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contemporary 记成 con（一起）加 tempor（时间）加 ary：和你共享同一段时间的，就是同时代的、当代的。

root: 源自拉丁语 contemporarius（com 一起 + tempus 时间），本义是共处同一时间，后指当代的、同时代的与同时代的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the art of our own day, to two lives in one century, and to the person who stood beside a famous name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从我们这一天的艺术，到同一个世纪里的两段人生，最后到站在名人身边的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a modern chair standing under an old timber beam.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把现代椅子立在旧木梁之下。

branches.en: The first sense points at the culture being made right now.
branches.cn: 第一个义项指向此刻正在被创造的文化。

branches.en: The second sense lines two things up in one period.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把两件事排进同一个时期。

branches.en: The third sense turns the period into a person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把一段时期变成一个人。

branches.en: Both senses depend on a clock everyone agrees about.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一个人人都认的时钟。

branches.en: A contemporary is a witness who happened to share the years.
branches.cn: 同时代人就是一个恰好共享那些年份的见证者。

intro.en: Contemporary is built on Latin com-, together, plus tempus, time, with the ending -ary.
intro.cn: contemporary 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、tempus（时间）与词尾 -ary 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin time base tempor- also appears in temporary, tempo and temporal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的时间词基 tempor- 也出现在 temporary、tempo 与 temporal 中。

items.exampleCN: 这两位作家是同时代人。
这两份记录属于同一时期。

items.meaning: in the manner of the present time
items.exampleCN: 这座大厅采用了当代风格。

items.meaning: the speed of a piece of music
items.example: The tempo slowed near the end.
items.exampleCN: 曲子在结尾处慢了下来。

items.meaning: relating to time or worldly life
items.meaningCN: 与时间或世俗生活有关的
items.example: The essay deals with temporal change.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章讨论时间中的变化。

items.meaning: to delay in order to gain time
spoken without preparation, on the spot
items.meaningCN: 当场说出而未经准备的

definition_zh: 预定的；到期的；应付的；由于；应有的；应得之物
definition_en: expected or scheduled to happen, owed or payable, caused by, rightly required, or the share that is owed to someone
core_image: 日历上一格被圈住的日子，旁边压着一张未付的账单
scene: 站台上的电子屏一遍遍刷新到达时间，人群开始向前挪。 The next train is due in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 due 是「预定到达的」（第 1 个义项：按时刻表预期发生或到达）；句意是下一班火车预定十分钟后到达。

pos.zh: 形容词：预定的；到期的；应付的；由于；应有的
名词：应得之物；应得的份额

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「按时地；适当地」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「过分的；不应有的」
由前缀 over- 加本词构成，义为「过期的；迟到的」
与 due 同出拉丁语 debere，义为「义务；职责；税」

senses.title: Expected or scheduled
senses.definition: expected or arranged to happen or arrive at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 预期或安排在某时发生、到达
senses.example: The train is due at six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车预定六点到。
senses.why: Something due is placed on a timetable; the word marks a point that has been fixed in advance and is now being approached.
senses.whyCN: 事情被放进时刻表，due 标出一个预先定好、正在逐渐临近的时点。

senses.title: Owed or payable
senses.definition: owed as money or as a right, and therefore required to be paid or given
senses.definitionCN: 作为钱款或权利而欠下的，因此必须支付或给予
senses.example: The rent is due on the first of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 房租在每月一号到期。
senses.why: The oldest sense is debt: what one owes has a date attached, so due moves from 'owed' to 'payable now'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是债务：欠下的东西带着一个日期，所以 due 从「欠着」走到「现在该付」。

senses.title: Caused by
senses.definition: used in the phrase due to to mean caused by or because of
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 due to，意为「由……造成」或「因为」
senses.example: The delay was due to heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 延误是由于大雪造成的。
senses.why: If a result is owed to a cause, the debt image explains the cause: the effect is what the cause has produced and must be credited with.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果欠着某个原因，债务意象就解释了原因：结果是原因所产生、并应记在原因账上的东西。

senses.title: Rightly required
senses.definition: proper, adequate or rightly required, as in due care or due process
senses.definitionCN: 恰当的、足够的或理应要求的，如应有的谨慎或正当程序
senses.example: The doctor acted with due care.
senses.exampleCN: 医生以应有的谨慎行事。
senses.why: What is owed can also be what is owed by duty rather than money: the care a situation rightly demands.
senses.whyCN: 所欠之物也可以是责任而非金钱所欠的：某种情形理应要求的谨慎。

senses.title: A deserved share
senses.definition: the share or recognition that is rightly owed to a person, especially in the phrase give someone their due
senses.definitionCN: 理应给予某人的份额或认可，尤用于短语 give someone their due
senses.example: Give him his due: he warned us early.
senses.exampleCN: 说句公道话：他早就警告过我们。
senses.why: The noun keeps the debt image in human form: recognition is something owed to a person and can be handed over.
senses.whyCN: 名词把债务意象保留在人的层面：认可是一种欠着某人的东西，可以被交还给他。

intro.en: Due comes from Latin debere, to owe, through Old French; the modern senses all grow out of the idea of a debt with a date.
intro.cn: due 经由古法语来自拉丁语 debere（欠），现代各个义项都从「带日期的债务」这一观念生长出来。

items.en: Latin debere meant to owe or to be under an obligation, and it is the root of debit, debt and duty as well.
items.cn: 拉丁语 debere 意为「欠」或「负有义务」，也是 debit、debt、duty 的词根。

items.en: The past participle debitum meant something owed, and it became the Latin noun for a debt.
items.cn: 过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，后来成为拉丁语中表示债务的名词。

items.en: Old French deu, the past participle of devoir, carried the sense of owed and of fitting or proper.
items.cn: 古法语 deu 是 devoir 的过去分词，兼具「所欠的」与「合适的、应有的」两层意思。

items.en: Middle English dewe already meant owed, payable and proper, so the money and duty senses arrived together.
items.cn: 中古英语 dewe 已同时表示「所欠的、应付的、恰当的」，金钱义与责任义是一起进来的。

items.en: The caused-by sense of due to is often dated to the nineteenth century; its earlier history is debated.
items.cn: due to 表「由于」的用法常被定在十九世纪，其更早的历史仍有争议。

items.en: Due date, due process and give someone their due keep the debt image in law, business and everyday fairness.
items.cn: due date、due process 与 give someone their due 让债务意象继续活在法律、商业与日常的公道里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin debt family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of obligation, expectation and payment.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「债务」词族的词；近义组收表示义务、预期与付款的形容词。

entries.definition: In the proper or expected way, or at the proper time; due plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「按时地、适当地」，由 due 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: More than is proper or necessary; un- plus due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过分的、不应有的」，由 un- 加 due 构成。

entries.definition: Not paid or done by the expected time; over- plus due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「过期的、迟到的」，由 over- 加 due 构成。

entries.definition: An entry recording money owed or paid out; from Latin debitum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「借方；借记」，来自拉丁语 debitum。

entries.definition: Required to be paid, especially by a stated date; the commercial twin of due.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应付的」，尤指在指定日期前支付，是 due 的商业近亲。

entries.definition: Not yet paid back; it states the debt without the timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被欠的、未偿的」，只说明债务，不强调时间表。

entries.definition: Thought likely to happen; close to due but without the fixed schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「预期的」，接近 due，但不含固定的时刻表。

entries.definition: Still to be paid, as in owing to; also used in the phrase owing to for because of.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尚欠的」，用于 owing to 时也可表示「由于」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the Latin debt and follow it into timetables, causes and fairness.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从拉丁语的「欠」出发，再跟着它走进时刻表、原因与公道。

normal.en: Latin debere is to owe; due is what is owed, whether money, time or credit.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 debere 是「欠」；due 就是所欠之物，无论是钱、时间还是认可。

normal.en: A due date is the day a debt comes calling.
normal.cn: due date 就是债务上门的那一天。

normal.en: The train is due at six: the timetable owes us an arrival.
normal.cn: 火车预定六点到：时刻表欠我们一个到达。

normal.en: Due to means caused by, because the effect is owed to the cause.
normal.cn: due to 意为「由于」，因为结果欠着原因。

normal.en: Give someone their due means hand over the recognition they are owed.
normal.cn: give someone their due 意为把欠他们的那份认可交还给他们。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar square circled in red, with a bill pinned beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上一格被红笔圈住，旁边钉着一张账单。

abstract.en: The same circle moves onto a platform clock, then onto a courtroom schedule.
abstract.cn: 同一个圈又移到站台的钟上，再移到法庭的日程上。

abstract.en: Due is time turned into an obligation: something will arrive, or something must be paid.
abstract.cn: due 是被时间变成义务的东西：某物即将到达，或某物必须支付。

examples.en: The train is due at six.
examples.cn: 火车预定六点到。

examples.en: The report is due next Friday.
examples.cn: 报告下周五到期。

examples.en: The delay was due to heavy snow.
examples.cn: 延误是由于大雪造成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: due 与 debt、debit 同出拉丁语「欠」：欠钱是到期应付，欠时间是预定到达，欠原因就是「由于」。

root: 经由古法语 deu 来自拉丁语 debere「欠、负有义务」，其过去分词 debitum 意为「所欠之物」，也是 debt、debit、duty 的来源。中古英语 dewe 已兼有「所欠的」与「应有的」两义；表「由于」的 due to 常被定在十九世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of due all turn one debt into a deadline: a scheduled arrival, money to pay, a cause to credit, care that is required, and recognition that is owed.
sensesIntro.cn: due 的五个义项都把同一笔「债」变成期限：预定的到达、该付的钱、该记在账上的原因、理应的谨慎，以及应得的认可。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circled date on a calendar with an unpaid bill pinned beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上圈出的一个日子，旁边钉着一张未付的账单。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: money owed and now payable on a stated date.
branches.cn: 账簿线：欠下的钱，如今在约定日期应付。

branches.en: THE TIMETABLE: an arrival or event owed to us by the schedule.
branches.cn: 时刻表线：时刻表欠我们的一个到达或事件。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: an effect is owed to the reason that produced it.
branches.cn: 原因线：结果欠着产生它的那个原因。

branches.en: THE DUTY: what a situation rightly demands, such as due care or due process.
branches.cn: 责任线：某种情形理应要求的东西，如应有的谨慎或正当程序。

branches.en: THE CREDIT: the recognition a person is owed and should receive.
branches.cn: 认可线：一个人应得并应当得到的认可。

intro.en: Due is a Latin-derived adjective; English adds -ly, un- and over-, and borrows the same root in debit and duty.
intro.cn: due 是源自拉丁语的形容词；英语加 -ly、un-、over-，并在 debit 与 duty 中借用了同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin debere and its participle debitum are recorded forms, so only the deeper Indo-European origin is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 debere 及其分词 debitum 都是有记录的形式，只有更早的印欧语来源属于重构。

items.example: The adjective carries both the debt and the duty senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时带有债务与责任两层意思。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: Duty comes from the same French branch.
items.exampleCN: duty 来自同一支法语来源。

items.meaning: an entry of money owed or paid
items.meaningCN: 记录欠款或支出的账项

latinEntries.meaning: to owe, to be under an obligation

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun from the participle of debere

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「按时地；适当地」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「过分的；不应有的」
由前缀 over- 加本词构成，义为「过期的；迟到的」
与 due 同出拉丁语 debere，义为「义务；职责；税」

definition_zh: 允许；准许；使成为可能；许可证；执照
definition_en: to allow something to happen or someone to do something; also an official document that gives you the right to do something
core_image: 一只手在闸机旁按下按钮，横杆抬起，让一个人走过去
scene: 停车场入口的栏杆旁，管理员把一张塑封卡片放在挡风玻璃后面，示意司机可以开进去了。 A resident permit lets you park here all year.
sceneCN: 这里是名词「许可证」（第 4 个义项：官方发放、允许持有人在特定范围内活动的证件）；句意为有了居民停车证，就能整年停在这里。画面里是挡风玻璃后的那张卡。

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词 permittere 的动作名词 permissio 演变而来，义为「许可」；与 permit 同源，名词形式不同
由词干 permiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「宽容的；放任的」
由词干 permiss- 加 -ible 构成，义为「可允许的」

senses.title: To allow someone to do something
senses.definition: to give someone the right to do something, especially through an authority or a rule
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过权威或规则给予某人做某事的权利
senses.example: The library does not permit food or drink at the desks.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆不允许在桌边吃东西或喝饮料。
senses.why: Latin permittere is per-, through, plus mittere, to let go: the word begins as a physical letting-through and ends as a social yes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 permittere 是 per-（穿过）加 mittere（放开），本义是让某物通过，后来才转成社会意义上的点头同意。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to make an action possible, said of conditions such as weather, time or money
senses.definitionCN: 使某个行动成为可能，多就天气、时间、金钱等条件而言
senses.example: The narrow road did not permit two cars to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路太窄，两辆车过不去。
senses.why: If a condition lets an action pass through, the same verb naturally comes to mean that the condition makes the action possible.
senses.whyCN: 如果某个条件让一个动作通过，这个动词自然就表示条件使动作成为可能，这就是从允许到使得以的那一步。

senses.title: To authorize formally, as a body does
senses.definition: to give official approval for an activity, often in writing
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动给予正式批准，常为书面形式
senses.example: The city permitted the closure of two lanes for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门批准封闭两条车道进行维修。
senses.why: Institutions need a word for the official version of yes and took over the verb that already meant letting through.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个表示官方同意的词，就直接沿用本来表示放行的这个动词，正式批准义由此而来。

senses.title: An official document allowing an activity
senses.definition: an official document that allows you to do something or to go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 允许你做某事或去某处的正式证件
senses.example: He was stopped at the gate because his permit had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口被拦下，因为他的许可证过期了。
senses.why: English turned the verb into a countable noun in the nineteenth century, so the permission itself became a piece of paper you carry.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪英语把这个动词转成可数名词，那份允许于是变成一张随身携带的纸，这就是许可证义的来路。

intro.en: Permit comes straight from Latin permittere, to let through; the noun use is a later English reuse of the same form.
intro.cn: permit 直接来自拉丁语 permittere（放行、允许）；名词用法是同一个词形在英语里后起的转用。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to release and supplied the core of many Latin verbs of letting go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放开，是许多表示放手的拉丁动词的核心。

items.en: Per- added the idea of passage, giving permittere, to let something go through.
items.cn: 加上表示通过的 per-，构成 permittere，意为让某物穿过去。

items.en: The noun permissio grew up beside the verb and named the act of letting through.
items.cn: 名词 permissio 与动词并行发展，用来指放行这件事。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century, at first in legal and official writing.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，最早见于法律与公文。

items.en: The countable noun for a licence appears in the nineteenth century, and compounds such as work permit follow.
items.cn: 表示许可证的可数名词在十九世纪出现，工作许可证一类的复合词随之而来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds relatives of the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group holds verbs and nouns of consent and official leave.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁动词的同族词；近义组收表示同意与官方放行的动词和名词。

entries.definition: The action noun of the same Latin verb; unlike permit, it is almost always uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁动词的动作名词；与 permit 不同，它几乎总是不可数。

entries.definition: Allowing much freedom and not imposing strict limits.
entries.definitionCN: 给予很大自由、不施加严格限制的。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule, a law or a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 规则、法律或标准所允许的。

entries.definition: A task given to someone and sent with them, from the Latin verb of sending.
entries.definitionCN: 交给某人并随之前往的任务，出自表示送出的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To let something happen without opposing it, the most general verb of this kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不加以反对地让某事发生，是这类动词中最通用的一个。

entries.definition: To give official power or approval for an action.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项行动给予正式权力或批准。

entries.definition: A document that allows an activity, usually after payment and checks.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某项活动的证件，通常需付费并通过审查。

entries.definition: To allow something, used above all in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事，主要用于日常口语。

normalIntro.en: One Latin verb of letting through gives both the act of allowing and the card that proves it.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个表示放行的拉丁动词，既给出允许这个动作，也给出证明允许的那张卡。

normal.en: Mittere is to send, so to permit is to send something on its way instead of stopping it.
normal.cn: mittere 是送出，所以 permit 是把事情放它走，而不是把它拦住。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the t: permitted, because the stress rests on the final syllable.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 t 写作 permitted，因为重音压在最后一个音节上。

normal.en: As a verb the stress falls on the second syllable, as a noun it moves to the first.
normal.cn: 作动词时重音在第二音节，作名词时移到第一音节。

normal.en: Weather permitting is a fixed absolute phrase meaning if the weather allows it.
normal.cn: 天气允许的话是固定的独立结构，意思是如果天气条件许可。

normal.en: A work permit, a parking permit and a residence permit are all papers, not acts of allowing.
normal.cn: 工作许可证、停车证、居留许可，说的都是纸面证件，而不是允许这个动作。

abstract.en: A permit is a small rectangle of card standing in for a person's word, so the gate trusts the paper rather than you.
abstract.cn: permit 是一小张纸卡，代替某个人的口头承诺，于是闸机信的是纸，不是你。

abstract.en: To permit is to step aside: the verb describes not doing something, and that is its whole content.
abstract.cn: 允许就是往旁边让一步；这个动词描述的是一种不作为，它的全部内容就在这里。

abstract.en: Every permit carries a boundary, saying how long and how far, which is why a licence can expire.
abstract.cn: 每一张许可证都带着边界，说明多久、多远，所以证件才会过期。

examples.en: Smoking is not permitted anywhere inside the building.
examples.cn: 楼内任何地方都不准吸烟。

examples.en: If the weather permits, we will hold the ceremony outside.
examples.cn: 如果天气允许，我们会在户外举行仪式。

examples.en: Her permit allows her to work in the country for two years.
examples.cn: 她的许可证允许她在这个国家工作两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼米特」——闸机前有人泼了一地米，特批之后才放你过去；permit 就是允许。

root: 拉丁语 permittere（per- 穿过 + mittere 送出）意为放行、允许；名词 permit 是英语后起的转用，与 permission 同源而词形不同。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin verb of letting through supplies both the act of allowing and the paper that proves it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示放行的拉丁动词，既提供了允许这个动作，也提供了证明允许的那张纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing the button beside a barrier so that the bar lifts and someone walks through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在闸机旁按下按钮，横杆抬起，让一个人走过去。

branches.en: a barrier lifting for one person
branches.cn: 横杆为一个人抬起

branches.en: a narrow lane where two cars cannot meet
branches.cn: 窄路上两车无法交会

branches.en: a signed order closing two lanes
branches.cn: 一纸批准封闭两条车道的公文

branches.en: a card checked at a gate
branches.cn: 在门口被查验的一张卡

branches.en: the same yes spoken once and printed once
branches.cn: 同一个「可以」，一次说出口，一次印在纸上

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin prefix of passage, a Latin verb of sending, and an English habit of turning verbs into countable nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词靠表示穿过的拉丁前缀、表示送出的拉丁动词，以及英语把动词转成可数名词的习惯支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is recorded without gaps: mittere, permittere and permissio all survive in English borrowings.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的拉丁来历有完整记录：mittere、permittere、permissio 都以借词形式留在英语里。

definition_zh: 棍；棒；枝条；手杖；粘住；卡住；坚持；容忍
definition_en: a thin piece of wood, or to become fixed to something and stay there
core_image: 一根捡起的枯枝插进雪里立住——插下就不再倒
scene: 雪后的公园里，孩子用树枝在雪地上画着大圈。 She drew a huge circle in the snow with a long stick.
sceneCN: 这里 stick 是名词「棍；枝条」（第 1 个义项：细长的木条）；句意为她用一根长树枝在雪地上画了一个大圆圈。

collocations.phrase: stick a poster on the wall

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「黏的；黏性的；棘手的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「黏性；黏度」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「贴纸；不干胶」

senses.title: A thin piece of wood broken from a tree
senses.definition: a long thin piece of wood, especially one cut or broken from a tree
senses.definitionCN: 细长的木条，尤指从树上折下或砍下的
senses.example: The dog chased the stick and brought it back.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着树枝跑，把它叼了回来。
senses.why: The branch planted upright in snow, still holding its tree shape.
senses.whyCN: 插进雪里立住的枯枝，还带着树的形状。

senses.title: To be fixed to a surface and stay
senses.definition: to be attached to something by gluing, suction, or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 因胶、吸附或按压而附着在物体表面
senses.example: The stamp would not stick because the envelope was damp.
senses.exampleCN: 信封太潮，邮票粘不住。
senses.why: The branch pushed into snow stays exactly where it lands.
senses.whyCN: 插进雪里的树枝停在落地之处，不再移动，即粘附。

senses.title: To be caught or jammed and unable to move
senses.definition: to become fixed in a place so that movement is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 被卡在某个位置以致无法移动
senses.example: The key stuck in the frozen lock.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙卡在冻住的锁里了。
senses.why: Pushed in too far, the branch will not come back out.
senses.whyCN: 插得太深的枝条拔不出来，即卡滞。

senses.title: To continue firmly with a plan or belief
senses.definition: to keep following a decision, plan, or promise without changing
senses.definitionCN: 不改初衷地继续执行决定、计划或承诺
senses.example: She stuck to her diet even at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在聚会上她也坚持节食。
senses.why: The branch stays planted through wind instead of falling over.
senses.whyCN: 枝条在大风中仍立定不倒，即坚持。

senses.title: To put something somewhere quickly or firmly
senses.definition: to push something into or onto a place, often quickly, as in stick a note on the door
senses.definitionCN: 把某物快速或用力推入或贴上某处，如把便条贴在门上
senses.example: Just stick your name here and sign below.
senses.exampleCN: 把名字写在这里，然后在下面签名就行。
senses.why: The planting motion, done with a casual hand.
senses.whyCN: 随手一插的动作，即快速放置。

intro.en: Stick is an Old English word for a thin branch, from a root of piercing or pricking.
intro.cn: stick 源自古英语，指细枝，词根一般认为与刺、戳相关。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stikk- is thought to mean to prick or pierce with a point.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *stikk- 意为以尖端刺、戳。

items.en: Sticca meant a thin stick or twig, a pointed little branch.
items.cn: 古英语 sticca 指细棍、细枝，即带尖的小枝条。

items.en: The verb of piercing gave the sense of fixing into a place, then of staying fixed.
items.cn: 中古英语由「刺入」生出「插入固定」，再引申为停留不动。

items.en: Stick to a plan borrowed the fixed image for loyalty and persistence.
items.cn: stick to a plan 借「固定不动」意象表达坚守与执着。

items.en: Adhesive uses, traffic jams, stickers, and sticky situations spread across daily speech.
items.cn: 胶粘、堵车、贴纸与 sticky situations（棘手局面）等用法进入日常用语。

note.en: Stick shares its root with stitch and sticky, and sits near different-root words for rods and clinging.
note.cn: stick 与 stitch、sticky 同根，义场靠近词源不同的「杆棒」与「依附」词。

entries.definition: a loop of thread in sewing, or a pain in the side
entries.definitionCN: 针脚；（肋部）刺痛；与 stick 同源于「刺」

entries.definition: covered with a substance that clings
entries.definitionCN: 黏的；由 stick 加后缀构成

entries.definition: a neat pile of things one on another
entries.definitionCN: 堆；垛；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a straight thin bar of wood, metal, or plastic
entries.definitionCN: 杆；棒，强调笔直规整

entries.definition: to stick firmly to a surface, or to remain loyal to
entries.definitionCN: 黏附；恪守，是 stick 的正式说法

entries.definition: to hold on tightly to something
entries.definitionCN: 紧贴；依附，强调抓紧不放

entries.definition: to let go of something held or stuck
entries.definitionCN: 释放；松开，与粘住相反

normalIntro.en: One image serves all senses: the branch planted in snow that stays, jams, and holds.
normalIntro.cn: 一个画面贯穿各义项：插在雪里、立住、卡住、支撑的枝条。

normal.en: Stick, stuck, stuck is the irregular verb chain to memorize.
normal.cn: stick—stuck—stuck 是需记住的不规则动词链。

normal.en: Stick to the plan is the classic phrase for persistence.
normal.cn: stick to the plan 是表达坚持计划的经典说法。

normal.en: Get stuck in traffic uses the jam sense everyone knows.
normal.cn: get stuck in traffic 用的是人人都懂的「卡住」义。

normal.en: A sticky situation is trouble that is hard to get out of.
normal.cn: a sticky situation 指难以脱身的麻烦局面。

normal.en: Stick together means to support each other as a group.
normal.cn: stick together 指团队互相支持、团结一致。

abstract.en: Push a branch into fresh snow and watch it stand alone.
abstract.cn: 把树枝插进新雪，看它独自立住。

abstract.en: Feel glue grab between finger and paper and refuse to let go.
abstract.cn: 体会胶水在指尖与纸间黏住不放的触感。

abstract.en: Picture a car frozen between two trucks in a narrow lane.
abstract.cn: 想象小车在窄巷被两辆卡车夹住动弹不得。

examples.en: He stuck the notice on the board with two pins.
examples.cn: 他用两枚图钉把通知钉在布告板上。

examples.en: We stuck to our budget and finished the trip under cost.
examples.cn: 我们坚持按预算行事，旅行花费低于预期。

examples.en: My sleeve got stuck in the car door.
examples.cn: 我的袖子被车门夹住了。

sensesIntro.en: From the planted branch grow gluing, jamming, loyalty that stays put, and the quick act of pushing something into place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从插立的枝条生长出胶粘、卡滞、坚定不移，以及随手插放的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch planted in snow that will not fall or pull free
core.cn: 核心意象：插进雪里、不倒也拔不出的枝条

branches.en: the wooden piece itself
branches.cn: 木枝条本身

branches.en: surfaces that hold what touches them
branches.cn: 粘住所触之物的表面

branches.en: wedged too deep to move
branches.cn: 卡得太深无法动弹

branches.en: loyalty planted like the branch
branches.cn: 像枝条一样立定的坚守

branches.en: the casual push that plants something
branches.cn: 随手一插的放置动作

intro.en: The prick-root family turns one sharp image into needles, glue, and grit.
intro.cn: 「刺」词根家族把一个尖锐意象化为针脚、胶黏与坚毅。

latinIntro.en: Stick has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: stick 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: thin wood; to fix or cling
a paper that clings to a surface
a sewing loop; a sharp side pain
to stick firmly; to stay loyal
makes nouns for things or doers

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「黏的；棘手的」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「黏性；黏度」

definition_zh: 黑暗；夜色；黑暗状态
definition_en: the state of having no light, or the time when night has come
core_image: 没有月亮也没有灯的深夜
scene: 屋里没有一点光，只能听见自己的呼吸。 The darkness pressed in from every side.
sceneCN: 这里 darkness 指「黑暗」（第 1 个义项：没有光的状态）；句意是黑暗从四面压过来。

senses.title: The absence of light
senses.definition: the condition in which there is no light to see by
senses.definitionCN: 没有可供视物的光线的状态
senses.example: The darkness pressed in from every side.
senses.exampleCN: 黑暗从四面压过来。
senses.why: It names a condition rather than a thing, which is why it has no plural.
senses.whyCN: 它命名的是一种状态而不是东西，所以没有复数。

senses.title: Night itself
senses.definition: the period or presence of night, when the world is unlit
senses.definitionCN: 夜晚到来、世界没有光的时候
senses.example: They set out under cover of darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着夜色出发。
senses.why: Night is darkness given a time and a name.
senses.whyCN: 夜，就是被安上时间和名字的黑暗。

senses.title: Evil or ignorance
senses.definition: a state of evil, or of being kept from the truth
senses.definitionCN: 邪恶的状态，或被人蒙住真相的状态
senses.example: The story is about light struggling with darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲的是光明与黑暗的搏斗。
senses.why: The oldest metaphor we have puts knowledge in the light and evil in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的比喻把知识放在光里，把邪恶放在暗里。

intro.en: Darkness is dark plus the Old English noun ending -ness, which turns a quality into a state.
intro.cn: darkness 由 dark 加古英语名词后缀 -ness 构成，把一种性质变成一种状态。

items.en: The ending -nes made nouns out of adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -nes 把形容词变成名词。

items.en: Deorcnes named the state of having no light.
items.cn: deorcnes 指没有光的状态。

items.en: The spelling settled as darkness and the word entered the Bible.
items.cn: 拼法固定为 darkness，这个词也进入了圣经。

items.en: Writers began using darkness for ignorance and moral evil.
items.cn: 作家开始用 darkness 指无知与道德上的恶。

items.en: Darkness now covers everything from a power cut to a fallen kingdom.
items.cn: 如今 darkness 从停电一直能说到覆灭的王国。

note.en: The look-alike group is a row of -ness nouns, and the meaning group names other kinds of shadow.
note.cn: 形近组是一排 -ness 名词，近义组则列出其他形式的阴影。

entries.definition: having little or no light
entries.definitionCN: 几乎没有光的

entries.definition: the state of being slightly wet
entries.definitionCN: 微微潮湿的状态

entries.definition: the condition of being unable to hear
entries.definitionCN: 听不见的状态

entries.definition: a dark and sad half light
entries.definitionCN: 又暗又让人难过的微光

entries.definition: the dark shape a body throws
entries.definitionCN: 物体挡光投下的暗形

entries.definition: the dark part of every day
entries.definitionCN: 每天天黑的那一段

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin where the sun has gone and end where the word turns into a moral.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从太阳落下去的地方开始，落到这个词变成一句道理的地方。

normal.en: Darkness is not empty; it is full of things you cannot see.
normal.cn: 黑暗并不空，它装满了你看不见的东西。

normal.en: Sound grows louder when darkness takes the eyes.
normal.cn: 黑暗夺走眼睛，声音就变大。

normal.en: The word has no plural because a lack cannot be counted.
normal.cn: 这个词没有复数，因为缺失无法计数。

normal.en: Every lamp is an argument against darkness.
normal.cn: 每一盏灯都是对黑暗的一次反驳。

normal.en: We call evil dark because we cannot see our way through it.
normal.cn: 我们把恶叫作黑暗，因为身处其中看不清路。

abstract.en: Picture a field with no moon and no houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一片没有月亮也没有房屋的田野。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held out and not finding the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸出去，却摸不到墙。

abstract.en: Picture a single candle carried into a large hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛被带进一个大厅。

examples.en: The darkness pressed in from every side.
examples.cn: 黑暗从四面压过来。

examples.en: The village sat in total darkness after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后整个村子一片漆黑。

examples.en: He waited in the darkness for the bus.
examples.cn: 他在黑暗中等着公交车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 darkness 记成「打黑尼斯」：dark 是黑，-ness 是状态，合起来就是黑成一片的那种状态。

root: 由 dark 加古英语名词后缀 -ness（表状态）构成，古英语作 deorcnes；中古英语固定为 darkness 并大量出现于宗教文本，十七世纪起引申指无知与道德上的邪恶。

sensesIntro.en: From a room with no light, to the night outside, to the dark we speak of in the soul.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有光的房间，到屋外的夜，再到我们说到人心里的那片暗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a night with neither moon nor lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：既无月也无灯的夜。

branches.en: The first sense is a condition measured by what is missing.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一种靠「缺了什么」来衡量的状态。

branches.en: The second gives that condition a time and calls it night.
branches.cn: 第二个给这种状态安上时间，叫它夜。

branches.en: The third moves it inward, where not seeing becomes not knowing.
branches.cn: 第三个把它移进人心，看不见就成了不明白。

branches.en: A power cut and a winter night produce the same picture.
branches.cn: 停电和冬夜造出同一幅画面。

branches.en: Night is when danger feels close, and the metaphor grows from that.
branches.cn: 夜里危险显得近，这个比喻就是从那里长出来的。

intro.en: Darkness is the noun of state built on dark, and it shares its family with the verb darken.
intro.cn: darkness 是建立在 dark 上的状态名词，与动词 darken 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -ness is Germanic, not Latin; the whole word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -ness 是日耳曼语成分，不是拉丁语；整个词都是英语本族词。

items.meaning: the state of having no light
items.exampleCN: 黑暗持续了好几个小时。

The sky darkened before the rain.
She smiled darkly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她阴郁地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: The cave was in pitch darkness.

items.meaning: darkness with no light at all

definition_zh: 中世纪的；中世纪风格的；中世纪式的（野蛮、落后）；中世纪的人
definition_en: belonging to the Middle Ages, or resembling the period in style, and by extension crude or backward
core_image: 一张泛黄的羊皮纸上画着带雉堞的城墙、修士与骑士，边角发脆，墨色已经被时间咬出小洞
scene: 修道院的抄经房里，烛光下摊着羊皮卷，抄写者正一个字母一个字母地描。 A medieval scribe copied the chronicle by candlelight, one letter at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 medieval 指「属于中世纪时期的」（第 1 个义项：时间上属中世纪）；句意为一位中世纪的抄写员借烛光逐字母抄录编年史。场景物件：羊皮卷、烛台、羽毛笔、窗洞；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 中世纪的；中世纪风格的；中世纪式的
中世纪的人；(复数)中世纪的文物与研究

senses.title: Belonging to the Middle Ages
senses.definition: dating from or existing in the period between classical antiquity and the Renaissance
senses.definitionCN: 属于古典时代与文艺复兴之间那段时期的
senses.example: A medieval scribe copied the chronicle by candlelight.
senses.exampleCN: 一位中世纪的抄写员借烛光抄录编年史。
senses.why: the adjective simply dates a thing by placing it between the ancient and the modern, which is what medium aevum means.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只按「夹在古代与现代之间」给事物定年，而 medium aevum 正是此意。

senses.title: Typical of the period's culture
senses.titleCN: 具有中世纪文化特征的
senses.definition: showing the customs, faith, dress or building habits of that period
senses.definitionCN: 表现出那一时期的习俗、信仰、衣着或营造方式
senses.example: The church keeps a medieval nave, a medieval rood screen and a medieval bell.
senses.exampleCN: 这座教堂保有中世纪的中殿、圣像屏与铜钟。
senses.why: culture, not the calendar, is being named here: the shape of an arch or a rite identifies the age.
senses.whyCN: 这里说的是文化而非日历：拱券的形状或一种仪式就标出了年代。

senses.title: Revived in medieval style
senses.definition: made in deliberate imitation of medieval forms by a later age
senses.definitionCN: 由后世刻意模仿中世纪形式而制作的
senses.example: Victorian architects added a medieval tower to a plain Georgian church.
senses.exampleCN: 维多利亚时代的建筑师给一座朴素的乔治式教堂加上了中世纪风格的塔楼。
senses.why: once the period was safely past, copying it became a style, and the adjective moved from origin to imitation.
senses.whyCN: 当那段时期安全地过去，模仿它就成了一种风格，形容词也从「出自当时」变成「仿其形」。

senses.title: Harsh and brutal, as imagined of the age
senses.definition: cruel or primitive in a way associated in popular memory with that period
senses.definitionCN: 以一种大众记忆中所认为的中世纪方式残酷、原始
senses.example: The sentence was medieval in its plainness: a fine, a whip and a wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那判决残酷得直白：罚金、鞭子与一堵墙。
senses.why: popular history reduced a long period to a single mood, and the adjective carried that mood into metaphors.
senses.whyCN: 通俗历史把漫长的时期压缩成一种情绪，形容词便把这情绪带进比喻。

senses.title: Backward or outdated
senses.definition: used of attitudes or systems thought to belong to a less advanced age
senses.definitionCN: 指被认为属于较低发展阶段的态度或制度
senses.example: The company's medieval attitude to leave kept good staff away.
senses.exampleCN: 公司那套中世纪式的休假态度把好员工挡在门外。
senses.why: the same historical distance now measures progress: to be medieval is to be behind, not merely old.
senses.whyCN: 同一种历史距离此时用来衡量进步：说人「中世纪」就是说他落后，而不只是旧。

senses.title: A person who lived in the period
senses.definition: a person living in the Middle Ages, used mostly in histories and in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 生活在那一时期的人，多用于历史叙述与复数形式
senses.example: The medievals counted years from creation, not from a birth in Bethlehem.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪人从创世而非从伯利恒的那次降生起算年份。
senses.why: the noun is simply the adjective standing alone, a common English shortcut for 'people of that time'.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是形容词独立使用，是英语里表示「那个时代的人」的常见省略。

senses.title: Objects or works of the period
senses.definition: collected medieval artefacts or texts, used in the plural by dealers and scholars
senses.definitionCN: 旧物商与学者用来指收集起来的中世纪器物或文本，多用复数
senses.example: The auction grouped the medievals with the early printed books.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖行把中世纪的器物与早期印本归在一起。
senses.why: specialist speech turns the adjective into a noun for the things themselves, so a category label becomes a shelf label.
senses.whyCN: 专业行话把形容词转成指物件本身的名词，于是分类标签变成了货架标签。

senses.title: Of medieval Latin or manuscript tradition
senses.titleCN: 中世纪拉丁语与手抄传统的
senses.definition: used of the Latin, script or textual tradition of the period, as distinct from classical forms
senses.definitionCN: 指那一时期的拉丁语、字体或文本传统，以区别于古典形式
senses.example: The glossary lists medieval Latin spellings beside classical ones.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词表把中世纪拉丁拼法列在古典拼法旁边。
senses.why: scholars needed a term for the period's own written language, and the adjective was narrowed onto the manuscript world.
senses.whyCN: 学者需要为那一时期自身的书面语命名，形容词便收窄到手稿世界。

intro.en: Medieval goes back to Modern Latin medium aevum 'middle age', a label invented by scholars to name the gap between antiquity and their own day.
intro.cn: medieval 可追到近代拉丁 medium aevum「中间的时代」，这是学者为古代与自身时代之间的空档所造的标签。

items.en: Medium aevum 'middle age' was coined by learned writers in the seventeenth century as a neutral dividing label.
items.cn: medium aevum「中间的时代」由 17 世纪的学者造出，用作中性的分段标签。

items.en: Medius 'middle' is an old Italic adjective, and aevum 'age, lifetime' supplies the time word; the deeper origin of aevum is not settled.
items.cn: medius「中间」是古老的意大利语族形容词，aevum「年纪、一生」提供时间义；aevum 更深来源并无定论。

items.en: English took the Modern Latin adjective mediaevalis in the early nineteenth century and spelled it mediaeval.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪初借入近代拉丁形容词 mediaevalis，拼作 mediaeval。

items.en: Twentieth-century printers dropped the digraph, so medieval is now standard while mediaeval survives in older titles.
items.cn: 20 世纪的印刷习惯去掉了二合元音，medieval 成为标准，mediaeval 只留在旧书名里。

items.en: The word also acquired a tone: to call something medieval can mean picturesque, superstitious or simply brutal.
items.cn: 这个词还带上语调：说某物「中世纪的」可以指如画、迷信，也可以指纯粹野蛮。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact year of the Latin coinage is undocumented, and the earliest English use is dated loosely to the 1810s to 1820s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：拉丁造词的确切年份无文献可查，英语最早用例只能约略定在 19 世纪一十至二十年代。

note.en: Group one holds the spellings and near neighbours of the same word; group two holds period words that are often substituted for it.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词的拼写变体与形近词；第二组是常被拿来替换它的分期词。

entries.definition: The pre-twentieth-century spelling of the same adjective, still used in reprints of old scholarship.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个形容词在 20 世纪前的拼法，仍见于旧学术著作的重印本。

entries.definition: The noun for the cult or imitation of medieval forms, so it names a later taste rather than a date.
entries.definitionCN: 指对中世纪形式的迷恋或模仿，因此是后世的趣味，而非一个年代。

entries.definition: A person who studies the period; the ending marks a person, not a time.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究那一时期的学者；词尾标出的是人，不是时间。

entries.definition: Built from middle and age but means 'neither young nor old' about a person, with no historical reference.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 middle 与 age 构成，却指人「中年」，与历史分期无关。

entries.definition: Covers the Greek and Roman world and earlier; medieval begins where ancient ends.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖希腊罗马世界及更早时期；medieval 从 ancient 结束处开始。

entries.tag: the high culture of greece and rom
entries.definition: Names the art and learning held up as models, which medieval culture was later said to have lost.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为典范的希腊罗马艺术与学术，后世常说中世纪丢失了它们。

entries.definition: A narrower word for land and service relations, not for the whole period or its art.
entries.definitionCN: 较窄的词，指土地与服役关系，不指整个时期或其艺术。

entries.definition: The pointed-arch style within the period, and later a taste for the gloomy and wild.
entries.definitionCN: 指那一时期内的尖拱风格，后来也指对阴森狂野之趣的偏好。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin components, real spellings and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁成分、真实的拼写与现代同族词。

normal.en: medium aevum 'middle age': the period sits in the middle, between antiquity and the modern world.
normal.cn: medium aevum「中间的时代」：这一段夹在古代与现代之间。

normal.en: The same media- appears in medium, median and intermediate, all 'middle' words.
normal.cn: 同样的 media- 出现在 medium、median、intermediate，都是「中间」的词。

normal.en: Two spellings are current in older texts: medieval and mediaeval.
normal.cn: 旧文本里两种拼法都在用：medieval 与 mediaeval。

normal.en: The family runs medieval, medievalism, medievalist, medievalistic, medievalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 medieval、medievalism、medievalist、medievalistic、medievalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases date the word: medieval history, medieval Latin, medieval manuscript.
normal.cn: 固定搭配替它定位：中世纪史、中世纪拉丁语、中世纪手稿。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with one long square greyed out between two bright ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一张日历，两个明亮的格子之间有一长格被涂成灰色。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning beside a page that curls at the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛在旁燃烧，纸页的一角卷了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a stone arch that is round below and pointed above.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石拱，下面圆、上面尖。

examples.en: Medieval walls still ring the old town, though the gates are gone.
examples.cn: 中世纪的城墙仍围着老城，只是城门早已不存。

examples.en: The museum labels the piece medieval, though its date is disputed.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这件器物标为中世纪，尽管年代仍有争议。

examples.en: Critics called the punishment medieval and demanded a review.
examples.cn: 批评者称那项惩罚野蛮落后，要求复核。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「medi」听似「没底」，中间一段没底的年月 → 夹在古代与近代之间的中世纪

root: 近代拉丁 medium aevum「中间的时代」= medius「中间」+ aevum「年纪、一生」；经近代拉丁形容词 mediaevalis 进入英语。aevum 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a date to a mood: a period, its culture, a later imitation of it, the cruelty and backwardness people read into it, and finally the people and manuscripts that carry the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个年代走向一种情绪：先是时期，再是时期的文化，再是后世的仿制，再是人们读进去的野蛮与落后，最后是承载这个名字的人与手稿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brittle parchment page showing a battlemented wall, a monk and a knight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张发脆的羊皮纸，上面画着雉堞城墙、修士与骑士。

branches.en: DATE AND CULTURE: one sense places a thing in time, the other reads the period's habits from the thing itself.
branches.cn: 年代与文化：一个义项替事物定位在时间上，另一个从事物本身读出那一时期的习惯。

branches.en: REVIVAL: a later age copies the forms, and origin becomes imitation.
branches.cn: 复兴：后世复制其形制，于是「出自当时」变成「仿其形」。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: the same distance that makes the period picturesque also makes it a byword for cruelty and backwardness.
branches.cn: 评判：同一种距离既让那时期显得如画，也让其成为野蛮与落后的代名词。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND OBJECTS: the adjective standing alone names the people of the period and, in trade talk, their artefacts.
branches.cn: 人与物：形容词独立使用指那一时期的人，在行话里也指其器物。

branches.en: MANUSCRIPT TRADITION: scholarship narrows the word onto the period's own Latin, script and texts.
branches.cn: 手稿传统：学术用法把它收窄到那一时期自身的拉丁语、字体与文本。

intro.en: Medieval is a Modern Latin phrase compressed into one English adjective, and its pieces also build other common words.
intro.cn: medieval 是把一个近代拉丁短语压缩成的一个英语形容词，它的各部分还构成别的常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius 'middle' also yields medium, median and intermediate, while aevum 'age' appears in longevity and in aevum-based historical labels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius「中间」还衍生 medium、median、intermediate；aevum「年纪」见于 longevity 及以 aevum 构成的历史标签。

items.example: The root places the period between two others.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把这一段放在另外两段之间。

items.example: The second element supplies the time span.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供时间跨度。

items.example: The suffix turns the phrase into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把短语变成形容词。

items.example: The medieval register is still legible.
items.exampleCN: 那本中世纪的登记簿仍可辨读。

items.meaning: the cult or study of medieval forms
items.example: Medievalism rebuilt the abbey in pointed arches.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪风用尖拱重建了这座修道院。

items.example: The medievalist read the charter aloud.
items.exampleCN: 这位中世纪学者把特许状读了出来。

items.meaning: in the manner of medieval scholarship
items.example: The essay has a medievalistic fondness for lineage.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章带着中世纪研究式的谱系癖。

items.example: The filmmaker medievalized the city with fake towers.
items.exampleCN: 制片人用假塔楼把这座城市中世纪化。

items.example: The mediaeval spelling survives in reprints.
items.exampleCN: mediaeval 这一旧拼法仍留在重印本里。

definition_zh: 东西；材料；填塞
definition_en: things in general, the material something is made of, or to fill something tightly
core_image: 一个塞得鼓鼓的背包，里面装着各种说不上名字的东西
scene: 他把衣服塞进背包里。 He stuffed his clothes into the backpack.
sceneCN: 这里 stuff 是「填塞」（第 3 个义项）；句意：他把衣服塞进背包里。

senses.title: Things in general
senses.definition: a word for things when the exact name is not needed
senses.definitionCN: 不必说出确切名称时对物品的统称
senses.example: Put your stuff in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 把你的东西放到角落里。
senses.why: This is the catch-all noun.
senses.whyCN: 这是包罗万象的名词。

senses.title: Material
senses.definition: the substance something is made of
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物的物质
senses.example: This stuff feels like wool.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料摸起来像羊毛。
senses.why: The general noun becomes a substance.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的名词在这里变成了具体的物质。

senses.title: Fill tightly
senses.definition: to fill something tightly with things
senses.definitionCN: 把东西紧紧地塞进某物
senses.example: He stuffed his clothes into the backpack.
senses.exampleCN: 他把衣服塞进背包里。
senses.why: Material pressed into a space becomes a verb.
senses.whyCN: 把材料压进空间，就成了动词。

intro.en: Stuff comes from Old French estoffe, material or cloth.
intro.cn: stuff 来自古法语 estoffe，意为材料或布料。

items.en: Estoffe meant material or supplies.
items.cn: estoffe 意为材料或物资。

items.en: Stuff named cloth and goods.
items.cn: 中古英语 stuff 指布料与货物。

items.en: Stuff widened to mean things in general.
items.cn: stuff 扩展为泛指各种东西。

items.en: To stuff meant to fill tightly.
items.cn: to stuff 表示紧紧填满。

items.en: Stuffed animals named toys filled with soft material.
items.cn: stuffed animals 指填了软材料的玩具。

note.en: Stuff is compared with look-alike words and with words for things and filling.
note.cn: 把 stuff 与形近词以及表示东西与填充的词作比较。

entries.definition: the workers of an organization
entries.definitionCN: 员工

entries.definition: to learn about something
entries.definitionCN: 学习

entries.definition: hard and not easy to bend
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬的

entries.definition: objects in general
entries.definitionCN: 东西

entries.definition: what something is made of
entries.definitionCN: 材料

entries.definition: to make something full
entries.definitionCN: 装满

normalIntro.en: Stuff is a word for what we have not named, and then for pushing it in.
normalIntro.cn: stuff 先是我们叫不出名字的东西，然后是把这些东西塞进去。

normal.en: My stuff is in the car.
normal.cn: 我的东西在车里。

normal.en: What is this stuff on the table?
normal.cn: 桌上这是什么东西？

normal.en: She stuffed the bag with books.
normal.cn: 她把书塞满了包。

normal.en: He really knows his stuff.
normal.cn: 他确实精通本行。

normal.en: The child hugged a stuffed bear.
normal.cn: 孩子抱着一只毛绒熊。

abstract.en: Stuff is what remains when names run out.
abstract.cn: 叫不出名字时，剩下的就叫 stuff。

abstract.en: A full bag is a small argument with space.
abstract.cn: 塞满的包，是和空间的一场小争执。

abstract.en: Knowing your stuff needs no loud voice.
abstract.cn: 真懂本行的人，不必大声。

examples.en: He stuffed his clothes into the backpack.
examples.cn: 他把衣服塞进背包里。

examples.en: Put your stuff in the corner.
examples.cn: 把你的东西放到角落里。

examples.en: This stuff feels like wool.
examples.cn: 这种材料摸起来像羊毛。

dict_mnemonic.text: stuff 本指「材料、布料」；后来泛指叫不出名字的东西，再变成动词，表示把东西紧紧塞进去。

root: 来自古法语 estoffe（材料、物资），经中古英语进入英语；由布料与材料，扩展为对物品的统称，再引申为把东西填塞进去的动作。

sensesIntro.en: Stuff is unnamed things, the material they are made of, or the act of filling a space with them.
sensesIntro.cn: stuff 是叫不出名字的东西、构成它们的材料，或把它们塞满空间的动作。

core.en: A backpack bulging with unnamed things.
core.cn: 一个被无名之物撑鼓的背包。

branches.en: A pile of belongings waits by the door.
branches.cn: 一堆行李在门边等着。

branches.en: A hand feels the cloth.
branches.cn: 一只手摸着布料。

branches.en: Clothes are pushed into a bag.
branches.cn: 衣服被塞进包里。

branches.en: Things are made of some material.
branches.cn: 东西总是由某种材料做成。

branches.en: Material is what gets stuffed.
branches.cn: 被塞进去的，正是材料。

intro.en: Stuff takes verb endings and builds noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: stuff 加动词词尾，并构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The source is Old French estoffe, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是古法语 estoffe，而不是拉丁语。

items.meaning: not fresh, hard to breathe in

items.example: The child loves her stuffed animal.
items.exampleCN: 孩子很喜欢她的毛绒玩具。

definition_zh: 访客、来访者；参观者；候鸟、季节性来客
definition_en: a person who visits a place or person, or a bird or animal that appears in an area for a season
core_image: 门口按下门铃的人：带着来意，短暂停留
scene: 前台登记簿翻开在最新一页，笔还未放下。 Every visitor must sign in at the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 visitor 是「访客、来访者」（第 1 个义项：到访某地的人）；句意为每位访客必须在前台登记。敲门的那个人，就是这个词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「拜访、参观」，是本词的动词基础
名词，义为「正式访问、视察」

senses.title: A person who comes to see someone
senses.titleCN: 访客：登门看望他人的人
senses.definition: a person who goes to see another person, especially socially or at home
senses.definitionCN: 去见另一个人的人，尤其出于社交目的或到家中
senses.example: Every visitor must sign in at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 每位访客必须在前台登记。
senses.why: The agent suffix -or turns the act of visiting into the one who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀 -or 把「拜访」这一行为变成做这件事的人。

senses.title: A person who comes to a place
senses.titleCN: 参观者：到某处游览或办事的人
senses.definition: a person who goes to a place such as a museum, park, or office
senses.definitionCN: 前往博物馆、公园或办公室等场所的人
senses.example: The museum greets two thousand visitors on a free day.
senses.exampleCN: 免费开放日，博物馆迎接两千名参观者。
senses.why: The destination widens from a person to any door worth entering.
senses.whyCN: 目的地从一个人扩展到任何值得进入的门。

senses.title: A temporary member
senses.titleCN: 外来者：临时加入的成员或选手
senses.definition: a person away from their usual team, school, or club, especially a visiting player
senses.definitionCN: 临时到访别队、别校或俱乐部的成员，尤指客队选手
senses.example: The visitors opened the match with a goal in the first minute.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在开场第一分钟就攻入一球。
senses.why: A guest on another's ground is still a visitor, even in a match.
senses.whyCN: 在别人场地上作客的人仍是访客，赛场上亦然。

senses.title: A seasonal guest in nature
senses.titleCN: 候鸟：季节性出现的鸟兽
senses.definition: a bird or animal that appears in an area only at certain times of the year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中只在特定时节出现在某地的鸟类或动物
senses.example: Winter visitors return to the wetland every November.
senses.exampleCN: 冬候鸟每年十一月回到这片湿地。
senses.why: Nature also arrives and departs; the season plays the host.
senses.whyCN: 自然界同样有来有往，季节扮演了主人。

intro.en: Visitor is visit plus the Latin agent suffix -or: simply the one who visits.
intro.cn: visitor 由 visit 加拉丁施动后缀 -or 构成：字面即「去拜访的人」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know, shared with vision and wise.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓，与 vision、wise 同根。

items.en: Visere means to go and look; visitare means to visit repeatedly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 visere 意为走去看；visitare 意为屡次造访。

items.en: The agent noun visitator names the official who inspects, especially a church visitor.
items.cn: 施动名词 visitator 指执行巡视的官员，尤指教会的巡访者。

items.en: The word travels through French forms related to visiter.
items.cn: 该词经法语 visiter 一族传入英语。

items.en: Visitor appears in English in both official and social uses, and later covers tourists and guests at large.
items.cn: visitor 在英语中先用于公务与社交场合，后泛指游客与来客。

note.en: Look-alikes keep the visit-root or the spelling; near meanings name other kinds of guests and arrivals.
note.cn: 形近组保留 visit 词根或拼写，近义组指称其他类型的来客。

entries.definition: to go to see a person or place; the act of visiting
entries.definitionCN: 拜访、参观；visitor 的动词与名词基础

entries.definition: the ability to see or an imagined picture
entries.definitionCN: 视力、想象；同出「看」词根，与 visitor 词根相同而语义不同

entries.definition: a movable face cover of a helmet
entries.definitionCN: 头盔面甲；与 visitor 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the winner of a contest
entries.definitionCN: 胜者；词根为拉丁 vincere（战胜），与 visitor 词源不同，仅拼写相近

entries.definition: a person who watches over an examination
entries.definitionCN: 监考人；同为巡视性质的人物，但词根是拉丁 vigilare（守望），不同源

entries.definition: a person invited to someone's home or event
entries.definitionCN: 宾客；强调受邀，visitor 不必然受邀请

entries.definition: a person traveling for pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 游客；只为游乐，visitor 目的更宽

entries.definition: a person who makes a short visit, chiefly British
entries.definitionCN: 短暂来访的人，主要用于英式英语

entries.definition: a person who has just come
entries.definitionCN: 刚到达的人；强调到达动作，visitor 强调探访身份

entries.definition: a bird or animal that moves seasonally
entries.definitionCN: 迁徙的鸟兽；与候鸟义相邻，强调移动过程

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built on visit plus the agent suffix -or.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，建立在 visit 加施动后缀 -or 之上。

normal.en: visit is the act; visitor is the one who acts.
normal.cn: visit 是行为，visitor 是做这个行为的人。

normal.en: -or marks the doer, as in actor and inventor.
normal.cn: -or 标记做事的人，如 actor、inventor。

normal.en: visitor center is the first stop for arrivals in a park.
normal.cn: 游客中心是来客在公园的第一站。

normal.en: the visiting team is called the visitors in sports.
normal.cn: 体育比赛里客队就叫 the visitors。

normal.en: winter visitors in birdwatching mean birds that come for the season.
normal.cn: 观鸟人说的 winter visitors 指按季节到来的鸟类。

abstract.en: A doorbell in winter dusk: someone stands outside with a reason to come in.
abstract.cn: 冬日黄昏的门铃：门外站着一个人，带着走进来的理由。

abstract.en: The guest book fills with names, each one a short story of arrival.
abstract.cn: 访客簿写满名字，每个名字都是一段抵达的小故事。

abstract.en: Birds crossing the sky in November are visitors the season sends.
abstract.cn: 十一月掠过天空的鸟，是季节派来的访客。

examples.en: The gallery counts its visitors with a sensor at the door.
examples.cn: 美术馆用门口的传感器统计参观人数。

examples.en: An unexpected visitor arrived while we were having dinner.
examples.cn: 我们正吃晚饭时来了一位不速之客。

examples.en: Summer visitors bring the small town its busiest months.
examples.cn: 夏季来客给小镇带来一年最繁忙的几个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「慰自特」——来访的客人自带慰藉，特意来看你。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 visitare（屡次造访）加施动后缀 -or。

root: 拉丁语 visitare（屡次造访）+ 施动后缀 -or（……的人）→ 英语 visitor，即「去拜访的人」。词根 videre（看）与 vision、view 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One suffix, one doer; the word widens from people who call on people to crowds, teams, and seasonal birds.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个后缀造出一个「人」：从登门的人扩展到游客、客队与候鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one who arrives to see
core.cn: 核心意象：为了看而到来的人

branches.en: The guest who comes to a person
branches.cn: 登门看人的人：访客

branches.en: The crowd that comes to a place
branches.cn: 到访场所的人群：参观者

branches.en: The team on another's ground
branches.cn: 站在别人场地上的一方：客队

branches.en: The bird the season sends
branches.cn: 季节派来的鸟：候鸟

branches.en: Every arrival signs the same book
branches.cn: 无论看人看地，每次到访都记在同一本簿子上

intro.en: The word is a small machine: root of seeing plus an agent suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词像一台小机器：看的词根加上施动后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin loved agent suffixes; -or is the classic doer-ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语偏爱施动后缀；-or 是经典的「做事者」词尾。

derivatives.zh: 正式访问，由 visit 加 -ion 构成
